articles.standfirst: Bet365 te ofrece el pronóstico del partido que enfrenta a Slovan Bratislava y Betis en el Tehelné pole correspondiente a la jornada 5 de la Champions League
articles.summary: Bet365 te ofrece el pronóstico del partido que enfrenta a Slovan Bratislava y Betis en el Tehelné pole correspondiente a la jornada 5 de la Champions League
articles.body: El Slovan Bratislava afronta esta quinta jornada de la Champions League en una situación muy delicada. El conjunto eslovaco cuenta sus partidos por derrotas y ocupa la última posición de la fase liga, siendo además el único equipo que todavía no ha conseguido puntuar. Su principal objetivo será ofrecer una imagen más competitiva ante su público y tratar de estrenar su casillero en una competición que se le está haciendo cuesta arriba. Favorito para el partido entre Slovan Bratislava y Betis El Betis, por su parte, vio frenado su excelente comienzo europeo en la última jornada, cuando cayó frente al Borussia Dortmund después de haber firmado tres victorias consecutivas. Pese a ese tropiezo, el conjunto verdiblanco se mantiene en la zona alta del Top 24 y tiene una buena oportunidad para acercarse a la clasificación directa para las eliminatorias. La diferencia entre ambos equipos también se refleja en las cuotas. Las casas de apuestas conceden un claro favoritismo al conjunto español. Bet365 ofrece una cuota de 11.00 por la victoria del Slovan, 6.50 por el empate y 1.25 por el triunfo del Betis. Ambos equipos marcan El mercado de ambos equipos marcan presenta algunos matices en la trayectoria europea de ambos conjuntos y ofrece una alternativa interesante para las apuestas deportivas. El Slovan Bratislava ha encajado goles en todos sus partidos de esta Champions, aunque solamente consiguió marcar en su estreno frente al Paris Saint-Germain. El Betis, en cambio, ha visto portería en todos sus encuentros, pero únicamente logró mantener su portería a cero ante el Feyenoord. Estos registros dibujan un escenario en el que el conjunto verdiblanco parte con ventaja... aunque los problemas defensivos de ambos pueden abrir la puerta a que los dos equipos marquen. Bet365 ofrece una cuota de 1.75 por el 'sí' y de 2.00 por el 'no'. Número total de goles (Over/Under) Los registros del Slovan Bratislava apuntan a un partido con posibilidades de superar los 2.5 goles totales. Todos sus encuentros en esta Champions han terminado con más de dos tantos y acumula 17 goles encajados en cuatro jornadas, una cifra que refleja sus dificultades defensivas. El Betis también presenta una tendencia favorable al over, ya que esta línea se ha superado en tres de sus cuatro compromisos. La única excepción fue su victoria por la mínima ante el Feyenoord. Con estos antecedentes, el mercado de goles ofrece una alternativa a tener en cuenta. Bet365 paga a 1.36 que se marquen más de 2.5 goles y a 3.20 que haya menos de 2.5 tantos. Número total de córners (Over/Under) El mercado de córners presenta una previsión más contenida si se atiende a los promedios de ambos equipos. El Slovan Bratislava apenas registra 1.5 saques de esquina por partido en esta Champions, mientras que el Betis alcanza los 4.8. La suma de ambos promedios se sitúa ligeramente por encima de los seis córners, por lo que la línea propuesta por Bet365 queda muy cerca de sus registros habituales. La cuota para que se superen los seis saques de esquina es de 1.12, mientras que el 'under' se paga a 11.00.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Stock Report: Jonah Coleman looking like league-winning back after 3-TD performance in Week 11
articles.summary: Matt Okada highlights his top risers and fallers for fantasy football coming out of Week 11.
articles.body:
As I write this on Sunday night, 12 of 13 Week 11 games are in the books (with Monday night remaining) and the fantasy football season is now past the halfway point. Still, things are changing every week. Promising improvements. Concerning trends. Performances that change our early outlook on players and teams. As always, some of these shifting perspectives will have permanent ramifications in fantasy.

With that in mind, I've compiled another full fantasy stock report. These are the most notable risers and fallers heading into Week 12.

Barring something extraordinary, Jonah Coleman has locked down the award for Waiver Wire Pickup of the Year. He scored a monster 32.9 fantasy points on Sunday, taking 24 carries for 111 yards and three touchdowns while adding four catches for 18 yards. That makes three straight games with 15+ touches and more touches in every successive game since returning from injury in Week 7. He's become a legitimate bell-cow back for Denver, a winning team with a strong defense, and has an excellent schedule down the stretch as well. There's no longer a question on whether Coleman will remain a weekly fantasy starter — now the question is whether he'll be a high-end RB2 or a low-end RB1 for the rest of the season. Honestly, with the volume he's accumulated and the impact he's had with that volume, I'd lean towards the latter. If you added him earlier this season — or were smart enough to draft and hold him — congratulations. You got a league-winner.

RB Travis Etienne Jr., New Orleans Saints

In Travis Etienne Jr.'s first week back from injury, the usage split with Audric Estimé and Alvin Kamara was extremely discouraging. He saw just eight carries to Estimé's seven and was matched at three catches by Kamara, while playing just 34.4% of the snaps. However, things changed dramatically this past Sunday against the Bears. Etienne shouldered 14 carries, while no other running back had more than one, and managed 5.4 yards per carry for a total of 76 yards.

Now, he was mostly uninvolved as a receiver and Kamara vultured another touchdown from the goal line, so it seems like Etienne's upside will still be capped much lower than we might have hoped when New Orleans signed him in the offseason. But, at the very least, he's back to being the RB1 for the team. And he'll have several much easier matchups than Jeffery Simmons and the Bears in the near future, including the Panthers in Week 14 and the Falcons in the fantasy championship. He's probably a borderline RB2 moving forward, but that's legitimately the best outlook he's had since Week 1.

A week ago, Chris Olave took the biggest stock dip of the 2026 season, when he was massively outproduced by rookie Jordyn Tyson and finished with just three catches for 30 yards on four targets against the Panthers. The dip didn't last long. Against the Bears on Sunday, Olave saw 15 targets and caught nine of them for 102 yards. It was his seventh game of the season with double-digit targets and his most catches since Week 3 and most yards since Week 4.

Incidentally, it was Tyson who disappeared in this one (with just one catch on two targets) and Devaughn Vele who stepped up in his stead (with seven catches on seven targets). Ultimately, the most reasonable takeaway here is that Olave is still, and should continue to remain, the New Orleans WR1, despite the spotty breakout from Tyson. Poor play from Tyler Shough and a mixed set of matchups down the road keep Olave from fantasy WR1 territory — as evidenced by his four-game stretch without a touchdown — but reclaiming his spot atop the pecking order should lock Olave back in as a WR2 for the remainder of the season.

As odd as it may be, there's a viable fantasy running back behind Derrick Henry right now. Justice Hill took six carries for 69 yards and a touchdown on Sunday, while adding four catches for 27 yards on five targets. It was his second game in the last three weeks with 15+ fantasy points, bringing his average over that span to 12.9 per game, and he's now logged 3+ catches in six straight games . Hill has been extremely explosive all year and is clearly the preferred pass-catcher out of the backfield. And with Jacoby Brissett at quarterback for the foreseeable future, we can expect the Ravens to trail more and throw more than they ever would with Lamar Jackson. Both are good news for Hill, who's shaping up as a weekly FLEX consideration. He won't be an RB2 with any sort of reliability as long as Henry is leading the backfield, but he's a fantasy contributor at a thin and ever thinner position.

Finally, after a nine-week stretch with fewer than 11 fantasy points every single week, Ladd McConkey returned to relevance in Week 11. He caught five passes on eight targets, and while he only managed 37 yards, he scored two touchdowns on the day, doubling his season total entering the weekend. It was a season high in targets and his most catches since Week 1, indicating that he's finally back to being fully healthy and involved as Los Angeles seemingly continues to turn its offense around (the Chargers have scored more points in three successive games, culminating in a season-high 24 on Sunday).

Obviously there were high expectations for McConkey and this offense entering the season, which has painted their struggles in an even darker shadow. But if McConkey's 18.2 fantasy points were an indication of a late-season resurgence, it's possible he'll finally return a little bit on the investment managers made back in the summer. Justin Herbert did end up in concussion protocol after this game, so hopefully he clears that protocol by next weekend ... especially given the matchup with the Patriots, who have one of the softest defenses for wide receivers this season. McConkey has easy WR2 potential in that contest, as long as everyone is healthy.

While the stock isn't cratering on Luther Burden III, given how consistently great he had been entering the Week 10 bye, that consistency is what made Sunday's disappearance so troubling. After three straight games with a touchdown, four straight with double-digit fantasy points and seven straight with at least four catches, Burden logged just two receptions for 10 yards on three targets in Week 11 (and added one rush for three yards). He also ran only 17 routes (fewer than Kalif Raymond's 20) and it felt worryingly like the first month of the season, when the Bears receiving corps was a convoluted mess and Burden was "just fine."

Also, it's not like the Bears were blowing the Saints out for the majority of the game, which might have explained the lower volume, they were just intent on spreading the ball around ... a lot . All this said, none of the Bears receivers leapfrogged Burden in any sort of meaningful way — Rome Odunze had just four catches, Raymond had one and no one had 60 receiving yards — so this can likely be classified as a fluke more than anything. Still, it was a reminder that this is an unusual offense with a prominent ground game, a ton of weapons and no real "alpha WR1." Burden should be fine down the stretch, at least as a fantasy WR2, but likely will not be a bona fide No. 1 with occasional duds like this.

After an incredible two-month stretch to start the season, in which he was the RB12 with 16 fantasy points per game, Jaylen Warren has now scored fewer than seven fantasy points in back-to-back weeks. After managing just 15 yards on seven carries in Week 10 (but catching five passes for 26 yards to sort of salvage the week), Warren had just 28 yards on nine carries on Sunday, with just two catches for one yard. It was his second game over his last three outings with a single catch — an aberration for him this season — and was his worst rushing output of the year by far.

It was also his second straight game with single-digit carries after hitting 10+ in every single game entering the Steelers' Week 9 bye. Now, the Steelers have also lost each of those last two games and there's arguably a bit of a chicken-or-the-egg argument to be made. Are they losing because they've changed Warren's role in the offense, or has Warren lost volume because they're losing? Either way, I'd expect him to bounce back, to some degree, but we may have lost the every-week fringe RB1 version of Warren that we enjoyed through the heart of the fantasy season.

Speaking of struggling Steelers ... DK Metcalf is officially a fantasy bust. He's managed a few random decent days — though he still hasn't scored 15+ fantasy points once all season — but those have mostly come on lucky touchdowns. He had 115 yards in Week 4 and then the one explosive game against the Buccaneers in Week 6, but otherwise Metcalf has been horribly inefficient and incredibly inconsistent as a result. He ultimately scored just 0.7 fantasy points with two yards on one catch this past Sunday, in an excellent matchup with the Eagles secondary, before being ejected.

On the season, his 48.6% catch rate is the worst among all players with 50+ targets, and his 1.3 yards per route run and 5.9 yards per target are both abysmal. He and Aaron Rodgers are on completely different pages, and with Roman Wilson back, Germie Bernard breaking out once again and even undrafted Max Hurleman showing out in Week 11 (no, I've never heard of him either), Metcalf is quickly fading from ineffective WR1 to offensive afterthought in Pittsburgh. He's scored fewer than seven fantasy points in three of the last four games. I would park him permanently on the bench and might even consider dropping him to avoid the temptation in the future.

We knew the Jaguars matchup would be tough for Cam Skattebo and the Giants run game, but 34 yards on 14 carries was particularly disappointing. It also didn't help that Skattebo caught just three of his seven targets (for 14 yards) and lost a fumble (a terrifying event for Skattebo fans and fantasy managers), ultimately finishing with just 4.3 fantasy points. While he has a good matchup with the Colts next week, Skattebo then faces the 49ers, Seahawks and Lions in three of the next four games, an absolute death row of defenses for running backs. And as Sunday's game showed, with the general inefficiencies of this offense, Skattebo is in danger of additional duds in these sorts of contests. While he was exceptional in Week 7 and 10, Skattebo has now scored fewer than eight fantasy points in five of his active games this season. It's likely to remain this hot-and-cold for the rest of the year, particularly against those tough opponents. One silver lining: if you can survive to the fantasy championship, he gets the Cowboys in Week 17.

articles.title: Blackhawks' Connor Bedard expected to miss 4 months after undergoing surgery on right shoulder
articles.summary: Chicago's young captain had returned to play in October after undergoing surgery on his left shoulder this summer.
articles.body:
Chicago Blackhawks captain Connor Bedard is set to miss several months after undergoing surgery on his right shoulder, the team announced Monday. The surgery, which was successful, is expected to keep Bedard out for approximately four months.

Bedard, who had only just returned to play after recovering from surgery on his left shoulder this summer , suffered the injury last Tuesday, while taking a faceoff in a 6-3 win over the Toronto Maple Leafs.

Early in the third period, Bedard's arm took some awkward contact, leading the 21-year-old center to double over and quickly leave the ice. Bedard appeared visibly frustrated as he headed straight into the tunnel.

Last December, Bedard had injured his right shoulder in similar fashion (on a routine faceoff) but had opted to rehabilitate it rather than undergo surgery. Blackhawks coach Jeff Blashill told reporters on Thursday that Bedard and the staff were weighing whether to go with rehab again or to opt for surgery, but had ultimately decided for the long-term benefits of the procedure.

Bedard's surgery this summer came after he injured his left shoulder with an awkward fall during offseason training. He was set to be out until this month, but was able to return to the team on Oct. 13.

This time around, the four-month timeline means that Bedard could return in March, with a few weeks left in the regular season. The Blackhawks, who sit at the bottom of the Central Division, are not currently expected to make the postseason, especially without Bedard — who leads the team in points despite missing the first seven games of the season.

Shortly after his surgery in July, Bedard agreed to a five-year, $75 million deal to stay in Chicago, making him one of the highest-paid players in the league. The 21-year-old center was named as the Blackhawks' captain before the 2026-27 season.

articles.title: Phil Taylor speaks on Luke Littler, crowds, and his sensational darting comeback ahead of MODUS Super Series return
articles.summary: Phil Taylor speaks to Sky Sports on his remarkable comeback to darts alongside Adrian Lewis for the MODUS Super Series; fans can catch every match of the MODUS Super Series from 23-28 November for free on the Pluto TV app or online at www.pluto.tv
articles.body:
The most decorated player in history will make a sensational return to the oche when Taylor joins up with long-time friend Adrian Lewis at the MODUS Super Series in his first competitive tournament in eight years, starting November 23 in Portsmouth.

The 16-time world champion has inevitably been compared to teenage sensation Littler - who already has two Alexandra Palace titles at 19 - but remains calm about the prospect of his world title record being overtaken.

"I have more publicity [now] than when I was winning it!" Taylor joked, speaking to Sky Sports. "Everywhere I go, people ask me 'do think he'll beat your record? It's all debating all the time.

"So just to qualify for the next 14 years isn't easy. He's got to keep his form going, he's got to work hard, and even then, it'll take 14 years - that's if he wins it every year!"

"If the crowds keep on at him, then he might just walk away."

Littler - the favourite in almost every tournament he participates in - has become something of a target of hostile darts crowds across the tour, even threatening to boycott future tournaments in the Netherlands after being booed and whistled during his defeat in World Series of Darts final in Amsterdam.

This is a feeling Taylor - who reached 14 consecutive World Championship finals between 1994 and 2007 - can relate to.

"I'm not a fan of it. I didn't like it when I was playing - it's the whistles," Taylor said.

"When you're in the venue, some of them are screaming and whistling and calling your every name under the sun. I have to go and get a dictionary when I get home to see what they were calling me!

"It is affecting him. He doesn't like it, and he doesn't deserve it in fairness.

"It's just something they keep saying you've got to get used to, but it's very, very difficult."

Taylor left professional darts in show-stopping fashion, finishing runner up in the 2018 World Championship after a sensational run to the final as the No 6 seed.

Could the adrenaline of competitive darts tempt Taylor into a sensational return to the Pro Tour?

"No - I'm 66!" Taylor said emphatically.

"I've still got my own teeth, I've got my hip done, got my eyes done - but no, not a chance.

"It would be strange for me anyway, because I don't play competitive anymore. Adie [Adrian Lewis], still plays and it's going to be different. I'm just trying and trying and trying to pick my form up.

"Age has caught up with me, that's the problem."

Taylor and Lewis representing England is an image which will bring back fond memories for fans of a pairing that has won four World Cup of Darts titles - the most by any two players in the tournament's history.

It was the opportunity to share the stage with Lewis once again that was the deciding factor in tempting "The Power" back to the oche for one last dance.

"It was the owner of MODUS, Jason Thame, who said I was playing with Adie, and I said 'yeah, I'd enjoy that' - that's why I'm doing it!

"I'm not as good as what I used to be. He's going to have to really play well on this tournament, but I'm going to go and enjoy it. That's the main thing. We'll have a laugh."

articles.title: Pau Cubarsí deja el CUPRA del Barça a su padre y conduce un coche más modesto: "Mis padres no quieren..."
articles.standfirst: El Golden Boy 2026, de 19 años, prefiere seguir los consejos de sus padres antes que conducir un coche llamativo. El Cupra Formentor que tiene asignado ha acabado en manos de su padre.
articles.summary: El Golden Boy 2026, de 19 años, prefiere seguir los consejos de sus padres antes que conducir un coche llamativo. El Cupra Formentor que tiene asignado ha acabado en manos de su padre.
articles.body: El flamante Golden Boy 2026, Pau Cubarsí, no responde al estereotipo habitual de las grandes estrellas del fútbol. El central del FC Barcelona y campeón del mundo con la selección española es uno de los mejores defensores del planeta, pero mantiene un perfil discreto y alejado de los excesos que, en ocasiones, acompañan a los futbolistas de su nivel. Y no solo en su comportamiento dentro y fuera del campo. También en otros aspectos de su vida cotidiana, como los coches que conduce para desplazarse a los entrenamientos del Barça. Porque Cubarsí no presume de superdeportivos ni de lujosos automóviles. Es más, ni siquiera utiliza el Cupra Formentor que recibió en virtud del acuerdo de patrocinio entre el club azulgrana y la marca española. ¿Y por qué Cubarsí no utiliza su Formentor? El propio futbolista lo ha desvelado en una entrevista con The Athletic: "Me gustan los coches y de vez en cuando miro modelos nuevos", reconoce. Hasta aquí, lo normal en un chaval de 19 años al que le gustan los automóviles y que dispone de recursos económicos más que suficientes para darse prácticamente cualquier capricho. Pero su idilio con los coches no pasa de ahí. Porque el joven central escucha los consejos que le llegan desde casa: "A mis padres no les gusta la idea de que, con solo 19 años, vaya conduciendo un coche extravagante". Sin duda, una forma de pensar bastante alejada de la imagen que habitualmente se asocia a las grandes estrellas del balompié. Y dentro de ese calificativo de 'coche extravagante' parece que en la familia Cubarsí también se incluye el Cupra Formentor VZ (un SUV deportivo de entre 272 333 CV), que no utiliza el futbolista, sino su padre. "Me dijeron que esperara un poco más, que me hiciera mayor y ganara experiencia", explica el jugador. Por eso, para sus desplazamientos diarios suele utilizar un coche más antiguo de la familia. Vamos, lo que hemos hecho muchos conductores cuando empezábamos a ponernos al volante... No es la primera vez que Cubarsí demuestra tener una relación bastante particular con los coches para un futbolista de su categoría. En una entrevista anterior con El Mundo, el central ya había explicado que compró un coche a sus padres y se quedó con el que utilizaban ellos. Una decisión que encaja perfectamente con los consejos que sigue recibiendo de su familia. También entonces reconoció que no tenía ninguna prisa por comprarse un automóvil de grandes prestaciones y que prefería esperar unos años, hasta contar con más experiencia al volante y con la aprobación de su madre. "Ya tendré tiempo de comprarme un coche de lujo", asegura ahora. Y razón no le falta. Con solo 19 años ya es campeón del mundo, ha conquistado el Golden Boy y tiene toda una carrera por delante. Tiempo para llenar el garaje de deportivos no le va a faltar. De momento, parece que en casa de los Cubarsí la última palabra sobre los coches sigue siendo la de sus padres.

articles.title: World Series of Darts: Dubai Darts Masters will to return to PDC calendar in 2027 after 10-year absence
articles.summary: The World Series of Darts will return to Dubai for the 2027 season; the Dubai Darts Masters has not been played since 2017; Gary Anderson was the last player to win the title in Dubai; watch the World Championship live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Dubai was one of the tour's original destinations and had previously hosted a World Series event between 2013 and 2017.

The World Series will kick off its 2027 season in Bahrain on January 15, before heading to the United Arab Emirates for the Dubai Darts Masters.

The tournament will see eight of the world's top PDC players battle it out in a 16-player knockout event between January 22 and 23 at the Coca-Cola Arena.

Scotland's Gary Anderson successfully defended his Dubai Darts Masters title when it was last held in 2017, beating Michael van Gerwen 11-7 in the final.

PDC chief executive Matt Porter said: "We're delighted to be taking the World Series of Darts back to Dubai.

"The city has a great history with the series, and Coca-Cola Arena will provide a brilliant setting for two days of top-class darts.

"We're looking forward to welcoming the world's best players and fans from across the region."

Eight first-round matches will be played on the opening night, before the knockout stages and the final are played on day two.

World Series ranking points will be up for grabs, as players look to secure their spots at the season-ending Finals in Amsterdam.

Ross Smith is out to defend his title after he thrashed Gerwyn Price 11-5 to become the 2026 World Series of Darts Finals champion in September, winning his second PDC major.

Sky Sports remains the home of darts with the World Championship (December 11-January 3) live. Stream darts and more through NOW with no contract.

articles.title: Northern Ireland Women: Can returning Kerry Beattie and Ella Haughey make an impact?
articles.summary: BBC Sport NI looks at Michael McArdle's decision to recall striker Kerry Beattie and the uncapped Ella Haughey to his squad for a friendly double-header against Greece.
articles.body:
Michael McArdle has decided the upcoming friendly double-header against Greece is the perfect time to bring back Kerry Beattie and Ella Haughey from the international wilderness.

Glentoran midfielder Chloe McCarron is also in under McArdle for the first time after a lengthily absence, but the Glentoran midfielder would likely have been included sooner if not for a spell on the sidelines through injury.

Beattie won her last cap a year ago while Haughey will hope to make a senior debut in one of the two games against Greece at Inver Park after she was an unused substitute in friendlies against England and Scotland in her sole call up in 2021.

The inclusion of both players, who have been in good form at their clubs, shows McArdle is willing to keep the door open for a return to the international squad if players are performing at club level.

Magill returns to NI squad for Greece friendlies

Portsmouth move 'great' for striker Beattie

Portsmouth striker Beattie has been in and out of squads since her debut in 2021.

The 24-year-old has four goals in 13 caps, the last of which she won against Iceland in the Nations League play-off a year ago.

A prolific forward during two spells at Glentoran, she has struggled for consistency in moves across to Scotland with the likes of Glasgow City, Hearts and Aberdeen.

She left the Dons in the summer and consulted with McArdle when deciding upon her next move, before joining WSL 2 side Portsmouth.

Beattie has eight goals in all competitions for a Pompey side languishing at the bottom of the table and McArdle is pleased she has settled in well.

"Kerry had spells at Hearts and Aberdeen and for whatever reason it didn't quite work out at both, she had good spells but not a consistent run to express herself," McArdle said.

"The move to Portsmouth, I was delighted she reached out to me for some advice, it's an alignment for her and it's been a great move on and off the pitch. It's allowed her to enjoy herself but also play 90 minutes and be that focal point striker.

"She will have been disappointed not to make the squad for the [World Cup] play-off [against Portugal] with her form but she worked hard and she's back in, I'm delighted for her."

Beattie faces stiff competition for the starting striker role from the likes of returning captain Simone Magill and Kess Elmore, who impressed in the last camp and scored against Portugal, but she should receive some minutes across the two games and will be keen to grasp her chance to make an impact.

West Brom defender Haughey's last involvement with NI came when she represented the under-19s in 2023.

A Lisburn Rangers player when Kenny Shiels included her in the senior squad as a 16-year-old, Haughey then moved to Nottingham Forest before settling at the Baggies, who play in the National League.

The left-back, 22, has been a regular this season for the club in the third tier and combines playing with her university studies.

Left-back has been a problem position for NI which McArdle has been trying to address as demonstrated by him bringing in Lucy-Jayne Grant in the last camp and Haughey for this window to allow Rebecca Holloway to play as a central defender.

Haughey will be competing with Grant to fill that full-back role on the left side and McArdle believes she is more than capable of doing so having tried to bring her back into the squad earlier in his reign.

"Ella's been at West Brom for a few years now. She has real potential, strong, athletic potential. We tried to call her up sooner but there were some challenges," he explained.

"She's probably been one of their top performers and one of the top performers in the league. Delighted she's earned this opportunity and hopefully she can make her debut and achieve her first cap."

McArdle has made a concerted to continue to widen the player pool available to him as he aims to build depth ahead of the Nations League campaign next year, but if Beattie and Haughey catch the eye it will show that giving chances to those previously involved under different managers could be another possibility.

articles.title: La despedida tendrá que esperar: Miguel Lamperti tendrá un último baile en Acapulco
articles.standfirst: El argentino, a sus 48 años, disputó el que parecía su último partido en Premier Padel tras caer en la primera ronda del Acapulco Major... pero tendrá una nueva opción como Lucky Loser
articles.summary: El argentino, a sus 48 años, ha disputado su último partido en Premier Padel tras caer en la primera ronda del Acapulco Major.
articles.body: Se marcha el primer gran icono que ha tenido el pádel. Miguel Lamperti jugó este lunes el que parecía su último partido profesional en la élite tras caer en el debut de cuadro del Acapulco Major... pero un Lucky Loser le ha dado una nueva opción de despedirse hoy ante Goenaga y Collado en dieciseisavos. A sus 48 años Lamperti disputa el cuarto grande de la temporada de Premier Padel y vivirá este martes su último encuentro poniendo punto y final a una carrera entre los mejores de más de 25 años y que le ha llevado a ser uno de los jugadores más reconocidos. Tras superar la fase clasificatoria previa y hasta dos partidos exigentes junto al también joven argentino Octavio Álvarez, al que dobla en edad, 'El Canoso' ha caído este lunes en su primer patido de cuadro ante el italoargentino Aris Patiniotis y el neerlandés Thijs Roper por 6-3 y 6-3. Un resultado que, lejos de empañar su carrera, pone en valor el carácter, la competividad y garra de uno de los grandes iconos del pádel que no conseguía meterse en cuadro desde el pasado mes de mayo en Asunción y que no ha dejado de intentarlo hasta su última oportunidad. De esta forma Lamperti dirá "adiós" al pádel profesional, pero no dejará de competir pues, en esta nueva etapa que compaginará con su paso a los banquillos para ser entrenador, Miguelito seguirá batiéndose en torneos de menor calado. Una despedida que ha recibido el cariño de todo el mundo de pádel que ha querido arropar a Lamperti en su úlltima gran batalla en pista reconociéndole como lo que es, uno de los grandes del deporte de la pala. Según la normativa oficial de Premier Padel, los lucky losers son aquellas parejas que, tras caer eliminadas en la fase previa, consiguen acceder al cuadro principal debido a la retirada o incomparecencia de otra pareja en su primer encuentro. Estos son los aspectos principales de su designación: Quién puede acceder: las parejas que hayan perdido o se hayan retirado durante la fase de clasificación. Criterios de selección: se tiene en cuenta, en primer lugar, la ronda de la previa alcanzada y, posteriormente, la posición de la pareja en la lista de aceptación del torneo. Bajas antes de finalizar la previa: si se produce una retirada antes de que termine la fase clasificatoria, todas las parejas eliminadas en la última ronda participan en un sorteo para cubrir la vacante. Además, se establece un orden de reserva por si surgen nuevas bajas. Bajas con el cuadro principal ya confeccionado: en este caso, la elección del lucky loser se realiza directamente en el club, siguiendo los mismos criterios. Por ello, las parejas deben estar presentes, firmar y permanecer disponibles. Varias vacantes simultáneas: si hay más de una plaza libre, se realiza un sorteo para determinar qué posición del cuadro ocupa cada lucky loser. En el caso de Acapulco, haber alcanzado la última ronda de la fase previa y quedarse a las puertas de la clasificación fue lo que permitió a Lamperti tener una segunda oportunidad y entrar finalmente en el cuadro principal.

articles.title: El Dépor confía en el ‘break even’ en 2026-27 tras apostar 12 millones al ascenso a Primera
articles.standfirst: El club gallego, de vuelta a LaLiga EA Sports, rozó los 25 millones de negocio en 25-26, con récord reciente en comercial
articles.summary: El club gallego, de vuelta a LaLiga EA Sports, rozó los 25 millones de negocio en 25-26, con récord reciente en comercial
articles.body: El Deportivo vuelve a donde su estructura le pedía estar. El club gallego ascendió este verano a LaLiga EA Sports y ya prevé conseguir la sostenibilidad económica por primera vez desde la pandemia. “El objetivo de este año es alcanzar el break even (momento o nivel de actividad en el que los ingresos totales igualan a los costes totales), con una masa salarial adecuada y lograr los objetivos deportivos”, avanza Paulo Dinis, director de estrategia y control del Dépor, en conversación con 2Playbook. Si cumple previsiones, superará los 60 millones de facturación en 2026-2027, la cifra más alta de su historia reciente. El ejecutivo lidera un área que mira al futuro con optimismo. El equipo coruñés rozó los 25 millones de euros de negocio en 2025-2026, todavía en LaLiga Hypermotion. En este punto destaca la pata comercial, que aportó un tercio de la cifra con 8,2 millones, récord de la última década, según datos extraídos de Intelligence 2P, la unidad de estrategia e inteligencia de mercado de 2Playbook. Esta partida es la más relevante del club y sigue impulsada por dos marcas gallegas, Abanca y Estrella Galicia, a la que esta temporada se ha sumado Nike, nuevo socio técnico blanquiazul, con contrato hasta 2031. Comercial facturó un 13% más interanual. Sin embargo, no fue la línea que más creció. La televisión le aportó 7,4 millones, un 18% más respecto a 2024-2025, y competiciones –donde se incluye el ticketing– disparó sus ingresos un 67%, hasta 2,8 millones de euros. La cifra de abonados y socios, tanto en número como en ingresos, también van de récord en récord en la era reciente. En 2025-2026, el Dépor recaudó 6,5 millones de euros, un 11% más interanual, con sold out de carnés en el Estadio Abanca Riazor. El feudo coruñés marcó la segunda asistencia media más alta de la categoría, con 24.247 espectadores en cada partido en casa. Los traspasos de futbolistas generaron un beneficio de 642.000 euros, ya que el club defiende su apuesta por retener talento en lugar de priorizar las plusvalías a corto plazo. Lo hizo en Segunda División, y lo ha logrado este verano tras el ascenso. La entidad ha conseguido retener talento pulido en Abegondo, como el de Yeremay Hernández, y “nos hemos permitido fortalecer”, reconoce Dinis, con una serie de fichajes en la que se entremezclan juventud (Lorenzo Amatucci, Bright Ede, Jonathan Asp Jensen...) con experiencia en la élite: Aubameyang, Adama Traoré, Leo Román o los cedidos José María Giménez y Marc Casadó. En cuanto al gasto, el Dépor ascendió la temporada pasada con una masa salarial de 21,6 millones de euros, un 60% superior a la de 2024-2025. La cifra es alta para Segunda División, pero desde la entidad defienden que la propia estructura del club “no se adecuaba a esa categoría; los gastos y el número de empleados ya miraba a Primera”. En este punto cabe recordar la importancia del fútbol base y del equipo femenino –que compite en Liga F– en la estrategia deportiva del club gallego. Por ello, los salarios deportivos se fueron hasta los 20,7 millones. A ello se sumó la cada vez más amplia plantilla de personal no deportivo: 5,4 millones se destinó a ella, un 20% más interanual, muestra del interés de la propiedad por consolidar un proyecto en la élite. De hecho, Dinis asegura que el trabajo y la inversión de estos años previos “nos ha permitido que al llegar a Primera no hayamos tenido que dar saltos en la estructura”. Además, jugar en la élite “nos abre otros horizontes en la parte de negocio”. El ejecutivo destaca que en Segunda la repercusión estaba más localizada en Galicia, pero ahora se abren más oportunidades para crecer en el extranjero. Volver a Primera División “nos abre otros horizontes en la parte de negocio”, reconoce Paulo Dinis, director de estrategia y control del Dépor Con esta exposición global y el fuerte apoyo local –el club cerró la campaña de abonados de verano con 29.854 socios, 4.000 más que en su última participación en Primera y ‘sold out’ en carnés con asiento (27.637)– “contamos con el presupuesto más alto de la historia reciente del club; y eso es importante, porque nos ha permitido construir una plantilla deportiva que opte al objetivo de mantener la categoría”, afirma Dinis. El pasado febrero, todavía compitiendo en LaLiga Hypermotion, el Dépor aprobó una ampliación de capital de 30,1 millones de euros, respaldada por la propiedad, Abanca y su presidente, Juan Carlos Escotet. Una nueva inyección que se utilizará para la mejora de las instalaciones del club: “Nos viene bien al límite salarial, pero el enfoque es las infraestructuras y así no entrar en endeudamiento bancario”, apunta el director de estrategia y control deportivista. El principal proyecto que tiene en marcha el club a nivel patrimonial es el Dépor Training Center. “Es la obra más importante del club en el siglo XXI”, aseguró Escotet en la presentación del plan inversor. En total, la renovada ciudad deportiva contará con 11 campos, ocho de ellos con las mismas dimensiones del Estadio Abanca-Riazor, y se construirá en diferentes fases para poder mantener activo Abegondo. “Estimamos que a finales de 2027 ya podremos concluir las principales obras. Ahora estamos con el nuevo edificio del primer equipo y el filial”, explica el ejecutivo. El Dépor Training Center cuenta con un presupuesto inversor de cerca de 40 millones de euros. “Abegondo es un consumidor de caja relevante en este momento, pero confiamos en que será clave en el futuro”, reconoce Dinis. En el estadio, el club ha sumado oferta premium en esta última temporada. En primavera estrenó dos nuevas zonas de hospitality (Club Riazor y Bar Bruma) que le permitieron volver a marcar un récord de ingresos por matchday en 2025-2026, con 9,3 millones. En esta parcela, la vuelta a Primera División “nos ha obligado a acelerar proyectos de hospitality porque creemos que nos ayudará a acelerar en ingresos”, apunta Dinis. articles.title: UK Snooker Championship 2026: Match schedule and how to watch on BBC TV
articles.summary: The 2026 UK Championship starts on Saturday in York - check out the match schedule, seeds, prize money, previous winners and BBC TV coverage times.
articles.body:
The 50th UK Championship starts at York Barbican on Saturday with England's Mark Selby seeking to defend his title.

Selby won his third UK title last year by beating 2024 champion Judd Trump 10-8 and, as the reigning champion, is the number one seed this year.

World champion Wu Yize and world number one Zhao Xintong, both from China, are the second and third seeds respectively.

Kyren Wilson has won the past three ranking events this season and arguably starts as favourite, although he is seeded eighth.

Ronnie O'Sullivan, who has lifted the trophy a record eight times, has had a challenging campaign and is seeded 13th as he seeks a first ranking title since January 2024.

The top 16 seeds will be drawn against one of 16 qualifiers, with the 128-player qualifying tournament taking place in Leicester from 21-26 November.

The championship is the first Triple Crown event of the season, with the other two - the Masters and the World Championship - both taking place in 2027.

The BBC has extensive daily coverage on BBC TV, while you can watch every shot of the championship on BBC iPlayer, the BBC Sport website and the BBC Sport app.

The match schedule, seeds, coverage times and prize money are listed below.

Ronnie O'Sullivan, John Higgins and Mark Williams - the sport's celebrated 'Class of 92 - are all in action at the event.

O'Sullivan won the first of his record eight UK titles by beating Stephen Hendry as a 17-year-old in 1993.

The Rocket, who will be 51 on 5 December, was the most recent of the three legends to claim the title thanks to a 10-7 victory over Ding Junhui in 2023.

The Englishman has not played many tournaments this season and has fallen down the world rankings, but can never be written off.

Higgins won the title in 1998, 2000 and 2010 - with all three of the Scot's wins coming against fellow 51-year-old Williams.

Welshman Williams won his two titles in 1999 and 2002.

The trio have won a World Snooker Tour title every year since 1993 - a remarkable run of 33 years - but have yet to lift a trophy in 2026.

The UK Championship, Shoot Out and Scottish Open are the only events left this year for them to continue their winning sequence.

Williams starts his campaign on Saturday afternoon, O'Sullivan plays on Sunday afternoon and Higgins has to wait until Tuesday evening.

The top 16 in the world rankings following the International Championship are guaranteed places in the last 32 in York.

Apart from O'Sullivan, there are eight other former winners in the top 16 - Selby, Higgins, Neil Robertson, Williams, Trump, Shaun Murphy, Zhao and Mark Allen.

The draw for the first round will be made on Thursday at 14:30 GMT during the final round of qualifying.

Three-time UK champion Ding Junhui will be one of the players hoping to qualify for York.

The 16 qualifiers will drawn to face one of the seeded players.

The prize fund has gone up nearly £300,000 from 2025, with the winner earning £312,500 this year.

O'Sullivan leads the way with eight titles, having won his first Triple Crown event in 1993.

O'Sullivan also lifted the trophy in 1997, 2001, 2007, 2014, 2017, 2018 and 2023.

Fellow Englishman Steve Davis has won the title six times - one more than Scottish rival Hendry.

Wilson, world champion in 2024 and Masters winner in 2026, would become only the 12th player to achieve a career Triple Crown if we wins the final on 6 December.

2023: Ronnie O'Sullivan 10-7 Ding Junhui

2017: Ronnie O'Sullivan 10-5 Shaun Murphy

There have been 23 maximum 147 breaks made across 49 previous editions of the UK Championship and its qualifying tournament.

Willie Thorne compiled the first one against Tommy Murphy in 1987.

Hendry and O'Sullivan are the only players to have made two, with Hendry achieving his 147s in 1995 and 1999.

O'Sullivan displayed incredible composure to make a 147 in the final frame of his semi-final against Selby in 2007. He made his other in 2014.

The 2012 championship featured three 147s with Andy Hicks, Jack Lisowski and Higgins all achieving maximum.

Australian Robertson holds the distinction of being the only player to achieve a 147 in a UK Championship final, doing so in the sixth frame of his 2015 triumph against Liang Wenbo.

Liam Pullen and Chang Bingyu, the 16th seed this year, made maximums in qualifying last year.

Schedules are subject to late changes. Seedings listed in brackets. All times are GMT.

13:00-23:00: Uninterrupted coverage on iPlayer, online and app

articles.title: Cody Rhodes vs. CM Punk Will Be Epic, Seth Rollins' Return Flop, WWE's Big Botch, More Raw Fallout
articles.summary: Ahead of Survivor Series this weekend, the Intrust Bank Arena in Wichita, Kansas hosted an eventful November 23 episode of Raw on Netflix.
articles.body:
Ahead of a major premium live event this weekend, the Intrust Bank Arena in Wichita, Kansas, hosted an eventful November 23 episode of WWE Raw on Netflix.

Royce Keys and 946 met Roman Reigns and The Bloodline one last time before they fight in WarGames.

After Rey Mysterio announced El Grande Americano for Team Mexico, Cody Rhodes countered with Seth Rollins for Team USA, causing friction with co-captain CM Punk.

Check out all the fallout from the go-home Raw to Survivor Series: WarGames.

CM Punk and Cody Rhodes Are Building Something Special

On paper, Team USA vs. Team Mexico was the most pointless match on the Survivor Series card, but CM Punk and Cody Rhodes have found a path to make this feel special.

In particular, both have thrived in the past week by leaning into the absurdity of building Team USA to fight their own friend, Rey Mysterio.

The SmackDown segment featuring Hacksaw Jim Duggan is the funniest moment WWE has produced all year, and the Raw segment was also excellent.

The growing tension between Punk and Rhodes could lead to a rivalry, but this could also set up the two to become a lovable tag team for a while.

Based on recent segments, that would be the best path forward, teasing an eventual heel turn from one of the two men on the road to WrestleMania 43.

Seth Rollins is back after over three months away from WWE, yet it does not feel like anything has changed for him in the time he was away.

In fact, it feels like The Visionary is all the way back to 2024 when he and CM Punk could not stand to be in the same room together while Cody Rhodes trusted Rollins fully.

After his failed heel run with The Vision, WWE has reverted to the fairly stale babyface role that had Rollins looking lost in early 2025.

While his appearance on Raw created a great moment of tension between Punk and Rhodes, Rollins' own dynamic with both men is tired.

WWE needs to find a quick character change for The Visionary that can make him seem like a big deal again.

A fast heel turn at Survivor Series could do the trick, but that seems unlikely.

For a full month, Dominik Mysterio has done nothing but beg to be on Team USA or Team Mexico, yet nothing was accomplished during that time.

He was repeatedly knocked around by both teams and was made out to be a loser who did not deserve to be on the Survivor Series card.

At the same time, Becky Lynch has repeatedly called out that Dirty Dom was one of the hottest stars coming out of WrestleMania 41.

WWE is aware that Mysterio was on a path to stardom, yet absolutely nothing has been done to get him back on track.

He is completely directionless, and that does not look like it's going to change any time soon.

What has Oba Femi done for the past month? As WWE builds toward the last big PLE of the year, The Ruler has spent weeks threatening to fight The Vision at some point.

The build to Survivor Series has put multiple big stories on hold, but no storyline has suffered more than The Vision vs. Femi.

Even with Bronson Reed injured after Crown Jewel, there is no reason The Ruler could not be directly interacting with Bron Breakker, Austin Theory or Logan Paul.

By leaving Femi stalling for time, WWE risks derailing his molten-hot momentum.

Three months on from his win over Brock Lesnar at SummerSlam, the hottest new star in WWE is just a guy, and his lack of usage could quickly cause fan apathy.

If the next big stage for The Ruler is at the Royal Rumble, WWE must find a better way to use the star. At least give him some short matches or a side feud.

Royce Keys Positioned For Career-Defining Performance at WarGames

Royce Keys is clearly the leader of The 946. His purpose in the group is to challenge the biggest star in WWE, Roman Reigns.

Inside WarGames, he can no longer simply talk a big game. He has to back it up inside the double cage.

Keys must be a monster threat on Saturday night. The goal should be to sell the 946 leader as a threat to The OTC at the level of his greatest rivals.

In order to sell that, Keys needs to perform at his highest level. He cannot let The Bloodline or even his own group members outshine him.

Reigns can help this by selling big for Keys, but the 946 leader's status will ultimately be defined by his own performance.

articles.title: 5 Trade Ideas for Auston Matthews Amid NHL Rumors
articles.summary: The Toronto Maple Leafs have the look of a franchise stuck in neutral, and it might be in need of some big long-term changes if things do not turn around in a significant way.
articles.body:
The Toronto Maple Leafs have the look of a franchise stuck in neutral, and it might be in need of some big long-term changes if things do not turn around in a significant way.

One of the big changes that could be on the table is approaching their two best players, forwards Auston Matthews and William Nylander, about waiving their trade protections. It has already been mentioned as a possibility, especially now that Matthews only has a year-and-a-half remaining on his deal.

If first-year general manager John Chayka and the team's ownership decide they need major changes, or fear Matthews may not re-sign, this would probably be the time to move him.

You do not want to wait until his final contract year, when he would be a rental.

You would want to do it when another team will have two potential playoff runs with him (at a minimum) and get maximum value.

We have already looked at some teams that could be a destination if it gets to that point. So now let's try to come up with some trade ideas involving some of those teams and a few others.

Players this good typically do not get traded unless a team knows they are not going to be able to keep them, or unless they request a trade and force their way out.

But we do have some examples of top-tier players getting traded in recent years, and what a comparable value might look like.

When Ottawa traded Brady Tkachuk to Florida this past summer, it received three first-round picks and a second-round pick.

Jack Eichel brought Buffalo a package that included Alex Tuch, Peyton Krebs, a second-round pick, and a first-round pick.

When Calgary traded Matthew Tkachuk, it received Jonathan Huberdeau, MacKenzie Weegar, Cole Schwindt, and a lottery-protected first-round pick.

Vancouver traded defenseman Quinn Hughes with a year-and-a-half remaining on his deal, acquiring center Marco Rossi, prospects Zeev Buium and Liam Ohgren, and a first-round pick.

In most cases, the boilerplate package for a top-line player is a good young NHL player, a top prospect, at least one first-round pick, another prospect, and perhaps another NHL roster player to balance it out.

There have also been a handful of high-profile "one-for-one" deals, including Taylor Hall for Adam Larsson and P.K. Subban for Shea Weber.

Toronto probably wouldn't be in the market for that sort of deal and would likely want several assets with long-term value.

So let's go with that when piecing together our ideas.

The trade idea: Chicago trades defenseman Sam Rinzel, center Frank Nazar, and two first-round picks to Toronto for Auston Matthews.

As Lyle Fitzsimmons noted last week, the Blackhawks need a superstar and an impact player.

They have salary-cap flexibility, trade assets in the form of young players and draft picks, and they might be able to put together an intriguing package that could get Toronto's attention.

Chicago's best player and biggest star is Connor Bedard, but he needs another star-level player to help take the pressure off and complement him at the top of the lineup (when he returns from injury).

Nazar is signed long-term to what should be a team-friendly contract and should be a strong middle-six center into the future.

Rinzel, meanwhile, appears to be breaking out this season and could be on a path toward becoming a legitimate top-four—or even top-pairing—defenseman.

It would give Chicago a long-term 1-2 of Bedard and Matthews, while Toronto could still eventually have Gavin McKenna as its superstar forward, with Rinzel potentially being an impact player on defense.

The obvious question, however, is whether Matthews would willingly waive his trade protections for a franchise that has been one of the worst in the NHL for his entire career. He's spent a decade without finding playoff success.

If he is going anywhere, you have to imagine it would be a team where he thinks he can win.

The idea: Rangers trade Gabriel Perreault, Cole Beaudoin, and two first-round picks to the Maple Leafs for Auston Matthews.

If a player on Matthews' level becomes available, you have to figure out that the New York Rangers are going to insert themselves into the discussion, whether it makes complete sense for them or not.

There is also an obvious connection between Matthews and head coach Mike Sullivan, with the two of them winning Olympic gold together at the 2026 Games.

The question would be whether the Rangers would have enough in the form of young trade assets to get Matthews.

Would the Rangers include Alexis Lafreniere in such a move? It might be difficult for the Maple Leafs to pry him away, given that Lafreniere finally seems to be breaking out and is signed to a long-term deal that could be very team-friendly.

Perreault and Beaudoin are two of the Rangers' better young prospects, with Perreault already showing he has some NHL ability and might be able to score at that level.

Beaudoin might not be more than a middle-six center, but he plays hard and brings some tenacity and aggressiveness to the ice. The Rangers have their first-round picks in 2027 and 2029, and there might be some value there, even if they are used as potential trade chips for the Maple Leafs to flip.

The problem for the Rangers would be the reality that if they do not trade somebody like a Lafreniere or Alberts Šmits (which they probably would not), they don't really have a lot of truly high-end players to offer.

Other teams could probably top their best offer.

The idea : Utah trades Dmitri Simashev, Tij Iginla, Jack McBain, and a first-round pick to Toronto for Auston Matthews.

Utah is an emerging contender in the Western Conference and might just need one player to bring it all together.

Logan Cooley looks like a burgeoning star, and adding one of the league's top goal-scorers to that lineup could be the type of move that takes them from rising contender to potential champion.

They also have the farm system to pull off such a deal with several high-ceiling prospects at a number of positions.

Utah has a handful of really high-end prospects in Caleb Desnoyers, Dmitri Simashev, Tomas Lavoie, and Tij Iginla, as well as four first-round picks over the next three years.

If Toronto could come away with two of those prospects and at least one of the first-round picks, there would at least be some big upside there long-term.

Simashev has already had a taste of pro hockey in North America, and it looks like he has a chance to be a really good defensive presence with enough offense to be a difference-maker and long-term cornerstone of an NHL defense. Toronto could use a young player like that.

The idea : Vegas trades Tomáš Hertl, Trevor Connelly, and two first-round picks for Auston Matthews.

Why Vegas? The better question is: why not Vegas?

You know the Golden Knights would be interested in a new big-name star, and it would be pure cinema to reunite Matthews and Mitch Marner.

Does Vegas have the prospect pool or draft pick capital (or cap space) to pull it off? You would think not, but it always finds a way.

To take on Matthews' contract, Vegas would likely need to move a big salary out. Hertl, 33, could be a candidate, particularly given his age.

Connelly is Vegas' best young player at the moment and has at least shown he has a chance to be an NHL player. Vegas has two first-round picks in 2028, and it has never been shy about trading any first-round picks it has.

The idea: Capitals trade Dylan Strome, Cole Hutson, Ivan Miroshnichenko, and a first-round pick for Auston Matthews.

The Capitals should be better than their record, and if Logan Thompson ever figures things out in goal, they will be.

If they are going to become a serious Stanley Cup contender again, though, they will need a star-level player somewhere on the roster.

They have a lot of really good players, and the whole could be greater than the sum of its parts, but they still need that star-level player to be the focal point, especially now that Alex Ovechkin has regressed and is set to retire after this season.

Strome would become redundant on a roster that would have Matthews, Pierre-Luc Dubois, and the potential of Ilya Protas on it, and would also help clear some salary cap space both this season and next season, while also giving Toronto a serviceable NHL center.

Hutson would be the prize of the deal, with a chance to be a top-pairing defenseman.

Miroshnichenko is already looking for a way out of Washington and would be a lottery ticket for the Maple Leafs to roll the dice on.

articles.title: Gerwyn Price: Four-time Grand Slam champion casts doubt over accepting Premier League Darts spot
articles.summary: Grand Slam of Darts champion Gerwyn Price hints at missing next year's Premier League Darts; you can watch the World Darts Championship live on Sky Sports from December 11
articles.body:
Price ended his major trophy drought by winning the Grand Slam of Darts with a brilliant 16-11 victory over Gian van Veen in Wolverhampton on Sunday .

Price claimed Grand Slam glory for the fourth time as he celebrated his first televised ranking title since November 2021.

The Welshman will be eyeing further televised success as the Ladbrokes Players Championship Finals takes place at Butlin's Minehead Resort from November 27-29 before the start of the World Championship on December 11 - live on Sky Sports .

Then all eyes turn to the Premier League where PDC chief Matt Porter recently teased a change to the format .

Price, a finalist in 2023, previously suggested he might decline an invite to the tournament, which runs across 16 weeks, after a difficult 2024 season before reversing his decision and accepting his selection.

The 41-year-old, who has hit five nine-dart finishes in Premier League Darts, the most by any player in the tournament's history, has now hinted at missing the 2027 roadshow.

Speaking on Sky Sports News, Price said: "My daughter's pregnant. I've got a lot of things on. It is difficult in the Premier League with World Series and how many events the PDC are putting on these days.

"It's a couple of months before things are decided for that. So we'll see how things go."

Price also spoke about Luke Littler facing repeated booing and whistling from crowds at major tournaments, with 'The Iceman' suggesting it will eventually "go away".

Price has been subjected to boos and he even wore ear defenders to block out jeers from the crowd at the World Championship in 2023.

"The crowd like to see the underdog win, and I think that's what Luke is going through at the minute," Price reflected.

"Obviously, being the best player in the world is what he is at the minute, and I think a lot of people are a little bit jealous and jump on his back because they want to see him fail because he is so successful. But that'll go away.

"I never thought it would go away with me, but it does eventually, and it will with him as well.

"He's a great lad, he's a great player, he's great for the sport, and people should just get off his back."

Sky Sports remains the home of darts with the World Championship (December 11-January 3) live. Stream darts and more through NOW with no contract.

articles.title: 7 Plan B Trade Ideas for NHL Teams That Missed on Dylan Larkin
articles.summary: Detroit's long nightmare is over at last after sending Dylan Larkin to the Montréal Canadiens.
articles.body:
Detroit's long nightmare is over at last after sending Dylan Larkin to the Montréal Canadiens.

Now that he and Connor Hellebuyck are both on new teams, we're left wondering about what's next. For teams that wanted Larkin, their attention turns elsewhere to find a veteran goal scorer.

For the teams that didn't land the 30-year-old center, finding another player to fill that need may not be quite as difficult as trying to pull someone with a limited trade list, but then again, some of the players that could be their next targets may also have trade protection to navigate.

Still, our heads stay up, and our eyes are focused forward on the next trade targets. There are plenty of teams who could use a lift, and not quite as many players out there who could be had. Let's take a look at who is and could be out there soon.

If the Penguins are going to be open for business, and by all accounts, it sounds like they are, a lot of attention will be paid to their biggest-name veterans to see if they'll be willing to go elsewhere for a shot at another Stanley Cup.

Buzz has been circling with Sidney Crosby already, but it's Evgeni Malkin we're keeping our eyes on.

Crosby departing the Penguins would be shocking, and it's not something we're anticipating happening, but Malkin has always had an air of mystery around him despite playing his entire career in Pittsburgh as well.

Malkin has long been mentioned in trade rumors, and the public pressure on the Penguins to bring him back this season was notable. That makes us think that if any of the Penguins' "Big Three"—Crosby, Malkin, and Kris Letang—is moved, it'll be Malkin.

That's not to ignore Erik Karlsson, of course, who is also in the final year of his contract, but we've resigned ourselves to believe he'll be playing somewhere new before the trade deadline in March anyway. But if Malkin goes, it'll be fascinating to see which contender steps up to add one of the game's greatest players of the past 20 years.

Elias Pettersson has been in trade rumors for a few years now, and even though he's got an $11.6 million cap hit through 2032, he's having a bit of a bounce-back season this year and has a history of being a high-end scorer when things in Vancouver haven't been bordering on disaster.

Pettersson's skill and hockey smarts make him a top player in the league, and there's no doubt that part of what goes through any interested GMs mind is how well he would perform away from a team that's struggled as much as the Canucks have the past few seasons.

Even though Larkin was traded with an $8.7 million cap hit through 2031, Pettersson's juicy contract would still be a difficult one to move, and that's before considering he has a full no-move clause. As much as Pettersson loves Vancouver, you wonder if their recent run of tough play, coupled with interest from a contender, might be enough for him to waive it.

One of the players who went to Detroit in the Dylan Larkin trade to Montréal was Kirby Dach. He's due to be a free agent in July, and if the Red Wings are looking to secure more futures, trading the newly acquired big forward might be in their plans.

Given that Michael Hage was the big pickup for the Red Wings in the Larkin deal, retaining Dach likely only comes with a contract extension, and with how tricky this season has already been for Dach, he might welcome that.

Then again, with where the Wings are organizationally after trading the former team captain, Dach may be open to going elsewhere, especially if it's a contender calling for him. After all, he got a good taste of the postseason last year with the Canadiens, and that is looking like a long shot with Detroit. With eight points in 22 games this season with the Habs, we'll be curious how he performs with the Red Wings and if he can remain healthy to take advantage of his new opportunity.

It seems that for the past few seasons, Ryan O'Reilly's name comes up when teams are looking for a veteran center who's a proven winner. The 2019 Stanley Cup champion and Conn Smythe Trophy winner is an obvious mark for trade talk, but with the Nashville Predators competing for a playoff spot and playing well so far this season, you wonder if that will still be the case.

O'Reilly is an obvious target for trade talk not just because of his proven history, but also because he's in the final year of his contract, which has a $4.5 million cap hit , and doesn't have any kind of trade protection. It's somewhat of a surprise he wasn't traded last season while the Predators struggled, but there's something to be said for appreciating a veteran player who'd rather stay where he is than pack up and move regularly.

At 35 years old, teams know what they're going to get from O'Reilly, and that he's still an effective player only makes him more desirable to other teams. But so long as the Predators are in the playoff race, it's hard to see them moving him.

With the Pittsburgh Penguins struggling terribly to start the season, GM Kyle Dubas may have a lot of work on his hands this season to change things up. One player who could be had is forward Rickard Rakell.

Rakell has another year beyond this one left on his contract with an affordable $5 million cap hit. With a history of goal scoring and solid two-way play, he would be an attractive player for other teams to acquire and one the Penguins would ideally be able to get a solid return on.

Rakell has scored 30-plus goals in a season three times and 20-plus goals three times as well. This season, he's got 13 points in 23 games with eight goals. There's no doubt a contending team would love to have a player like Rakell, but like many players, he's got no-trade protection according to PuckPedia.com . His eight-team no-trade list could hinder the ability to trade him

The Calgary Flames are down bad this season and very well could be (should be?) sellers this season. One player who could be had is forward Morgan Frost.

The 27-year-old forward is in the final year of his contract with Calgary, and his $4.375 million cap hit is more than affordable for any team. He had his best goal-scoring season a year ago with 22 goals, and historically he's good for around 40-50 points per season. As far as middle-lineup forwards go, he'd make a great depth addition for a contender.

Frost has done well with the Flames over the past couple of seasons, but if a team wants to add him, they'll need to not be on his eight-team no-trade list. With how tough it's been in Calgary, you'd have to think Frost would be OK with a change, particularly when heading into a new contract.

The Bruins are off to a great start this season, but even teams in good positions can still make a big deal with a player in a contract season, and the B's have a couple of them in Pavel Zacha and Casey Mittelstadt. It's Zacha who we're keeping our eyes on closely for a trade, however, because his two-way ability and how he's developed his offensive game in recent years make him an attractive player.

The Bruins have been aggressive with re-signing their own players (Fraser Minten, Morgan Geekie) as well as adding big-money players in trades (JJ Peterka), and with Zacha in the final year of his four-year deal with a $4.75 million cap hit and coming off a 30-goal season a year ago, that price is going up. Although the salary cap ceiling is also going up, with Zacha at 29 years old, you wonder if Boston would be eager to add another long-term, big-money extension to go with the others they've already got done.

Zacha is a valuable player, and his work on their second line with Mittelstadt and Peterka has been good, with 17 points in 22 games. But with the money they've spent on Minten, the hope they've got in Matthew Poitras, and the growth of James Hagens, you wonder if there's a move to be made here with Zacha to get something back for a player they may not be looking to extend.

articles.title: NHL injury update: What does Connor Bedard's latest shoulder surgery mean for the Chicago Blackhawks' 2026-27 season

articles.body: Connor Bedard's latest injury has been another big blow to the Chicago Blackhawks as the franchise announced their captain will miss some four months after undergoing surgery on his right shoulder. Bedard had been placed on injured reserve Sunday, with the organization recalling forward Dominic Toninato to address the immediate roster situation.Bedard sustained the injury on November 17 during Chicago's matchup against the Toronto Maple Leafs. The incident occurred early in the third period while he was taking a faceoff against Nick Paul.The Blackhawks captain appeared to experience immediate discomfort, striking his stick against the ice before holding his right arm and leaving the playing area for the locker room.The latest setback has renewed attention on Bedard's history of shoulder problems, particularly because injuries have affected both shoulders within a relatively short period.Last season, the center missed significant time after sustaining a right shoulder injury during another faceoff situation. His production displayed the offensive punch he still brings to Chicago's lineup.How will the Chicago Blackhawks manage the rest of the season?Now it’s on the Blackhawks to try to keep the team competitive without their captain. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: London Olympics medallist Gagan Narang and Archery Association of India's (AAI) Virendra Sachdeva filed their nominations for the Indian
articles.body: NEW DELHI: London Olympics medallist Gagan Narang and Archery Association of India's (AAI) Virendra Sachdeva filed their nominations for the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) president's post on Tuesday, the final day of nominations. They will contest for the top job alongside Fencing Association of India's (FAI) Rajeev Mehta, who had filed his nomination a day earlier.But the shocker comes not in the names that have entered the race but in the one name that isn't in contention: PT Usha. The incumbent IOA president and former track and field star did not show up at the office to file her nomination before the 4:30 pm deadline.PT Usha had found her way back into the electoral process after being nominated as the female representative from the Ice Hockey Association of India (IHAI). This came after she had finished fifth, outside the top four positions, as a Sportsperson of Outstanding Merit (SOM).With PT Usha staying away, the IOA will get a new president after the December 5 elections.On a day of frantic activity at the Qutub Institutional Area, former athletes and sports administrators filed their nominations in person.Mona Manish Shah, Ajay Patel and Vagish Pathak have sent in their nominations for senior vice-president's post.Vice-president's role, which will be filled by one male and one female in IOA's Executive Council (EC), has the candidature of Anju Bobby George, Sachdeva, Vijender Singh, Bhavneet Handoo and Suman Kaushik.Kamlesh Mehta, who came through as one of the four unopposed male SOMs in the electoral office, is the sole nominee for the treasurer's post.Sunaina Kumari, Purnima Mahto are the two contenders for joint secretary (female); Amitabh Sharma, Harjinder Singh are the candidates for joint secretary (male).Yogeshwar Dutt, Dola Banerjee and Rani Rampal have filed for the EC as SOMs.Narang a front-runner for IOA president's roleGagan Narang, who won bronze at the London Olympics in 2012, finds support from the government, it has been learnt, as well as from several other sections. With Gujarat gaining prominence in Indian sport amid preparations for the 2030 Commonwealth Games and its bid for the 2036 Olympics, the former shooter’s decision to shift base to Ahmedabad has also boosted his chances in the December 5 elections.Narang, who has nurtured many athletes since retiring, was also part of a five-member search-cum-selection committee for the National Sports Board (NSB).The 43-year-old Narang's candidature for the top job has been proposed by Kalyan Chaubey and seconded by Ajay Patel. Meanwhile Virendra Sachdeva, who is the likely challenger for the President's role, has been proposed by Banyala Harini and seconded by Rani Rampal.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: British Paralympic wheelchair basketball medallist faces 17 charges, including 11 counts of rape, over five-year allegations, remains in custody
articles.summary: Lee Fryer, a British Paralympic wheelchair basketball medallist, is facing serious criminal charges, including 11 counts of rape, stemming from allegations over a five-year period. His case raises significant questions about his athletic career and the ongoing investigations.
articles.body: Lee Fryer was part of the British wheelchair basketball team that achieved its best Paralympic result in 28 years at Paris 2024, winning silver against the United States. Two years later, the 26-year-old is facing 17 criminal charges, including 11 counts of rape, relating to allegations made by the same woman over a five-year period. He has pleaded not guilty to the charges, apart from one for which no plea was entered, and remains in custody ahead of his trial next year.Fryer faces 17 charges relating to allegations over five yearsFryer, from Pontefract in West Yorkshire, appeared at Leeds Crown Court on Thursday, where he faced 17 charges in total. These include 11 counts of rape, voyeurism, intentional strangulation, assault, controlling or coercive behaviour in an intimate relationship, possession of cocaine and perverting the course of justice.The rape allegations concern the same female complainant and cover a period between May 2021 and May 2026. The alleged incidents are said to have taken place in England, Spain and South Africa.According to the BBC, Fryer, who became a dad in February, pleaded not guilty to all the charges except voyeurism, for which no plea was entered. He is due to stand trial on March 22 next year, with proceedings scheduled to last seven days. He has been remanded in custody until then.Fryer was first arrested in July and was subsequently charged with possessing cocaine and perverting the course of justice, with the latter allegation relating to October this year. The court also heard that arrangements would need to be made to accommodate his disability during the trial.British Wheelchair Basketball and ParalympicsGB respondBritish Wheelchair Basketball (BWB) confirmed that Fryer was removed from the Great Britain programme and all its activities following his arrest in July. He was suspended pending an investigation, with the organisation's website listing the reason for his removal as a breach of its code of conduct.A BWB spokesperson said: "We are aware of the criminal charges brought against Lee Fryer and recognise the seriousness of the allegations."At the point of his arrest, he was removed from the GB Programme and all British Wheelchair Basketball activities, pending the outcome of the external investigation."As criminal proceedings are ongoing, it would be inappropriate to comment further at this time."ParalympicsGB also confirmed it was aware of the charges but declined to comment while the legal proceedings continue."We are aware there are charges against Lee Fryer."As the matter is now subject to ongoing legal proceedings we will not be commenting further at this stage," the organisation said.From junior international to Paralympic silver medallistFryer began playing wheelchair basketball at school before joining Wakefield Whirlwinds and later progressing to Sheffield Steelers. He earned his first international cap at junior level during the Under-22 European Championships before making his senior debut at the 2023 World Championships, where Great Britain won silver.His Paralympic debut came at Paris 2024, where he was part of the men's wheelchair basketball team that secured Britain's best result in the sport in 28 years. Great Britain reached the final against the United States but lost 73-69 after fighting back from a 12-point deficit.ParalympicsGB's profile of Fryer described the achievement as part of a landmark campaign for the team, which finished with the silver medal.The criminal charges have now placed Fryer's sporting career under scrutiny, with his suspension from the national programme remaining in place while the external investigation and court proceedings continue. He has not been convicted of any of the offences and the allegations will be determined at trial.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

At 20, both grandmasters are the youngest-ever contenders in a World Championship match, adding another historic dimension to the contest. Gukesh, who became the youngest undisputed world champion at 18 in 2024, will be looking to retain his crown against a challenger arriving in outstanding form.
