articles.title: Boy leads girls' team to third straight field hockey state title; coach (his mom) says Massachusetts hates her
articles.summary: Somerset Berkley won its third straight girls' field hockey state title with a boy scoring two goals, and Riley Gaines says girls deserve fair play.
articles.body: There doesn't appear to be any evidence that this field hockey player identifies as a girl. In fact, it seems he only competed with the girls because there is no boys' field hockey team at Somerset Berkley Regional High School in Massachusetts, where he is a senior. Under the state's rules, boys are eligible to compete on girls' teams if their high school doesn't offer a boys' team in that sport, and vice versa. So why did the opposing fans boo this boy every time he touched the ball? Because this has never been about trans hatred, but rather fairness. BIOLOGICAL MALE COMPETING IN GIRLS' CROSS-COUNTRY RACE DENIES ANOTHER RUNNER AND HER TEAM A TRIP TO STATE Let's get you up to speed. Saturday, Somerset Berkley won its third consecutive state high school championship in girls' field hockey, beating Nashoba Regional 5-4 in overtime. This almost certainly wouldn't have been possible without its sole male player, who scored two goals and has been named South Coast Conference MVP for girls' field hockey in consecutive seasons. What's more is that Ryan Crook's brother led Somerset Berkley to state titles in 2018 and 2019, and the team's head coach is their mom, Jen Crook. In Crook's 31 seasons at the helm, Somerset Berkley has won five girls' state titles with a boy on its team and none without one. How do you feel about that? This isn't an apples-to-apples comparison with what we've seen throughout high school sports in this country, where biological males are allowed to compete with females because of how they identify. Nobody can accuse this boy of pretending to be something he's not. But there are still a great many reasons why parents and competitors are likely fuming in Massachusetts — and none of them has to do with gender identity. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! For one, there is the Massachusetts rule itself. Few would object to a girl playing with the boys if she wasn't afforded an opportunity to compete with her own sex. It's for the same reason few would mind a 9-year-old prodigy playing up with the 12-year-olds. But a 12-year-old playing with the 9-year-olds? Now we have a problem. Folks have cheered on female placekickers and golfers who thrive among the boys because they're overcoming a biological disadvantage. But they're not so thrilled about a boy benefiting from a biological advantage — even if the rules allow it. And it isn't just about trophies. Three years ago, those Massachusetts rules seemed to play a role in a gruesome field hockey injury, when a different boy, playing for Swampscott High School, fired a shot that struck a Dighton-Rehoboth player in the face, knocking out two of her teeth and sending her to the hospital. The following season, Dighton-Rehoboth forfeited a game out of concern for its players' safety because the opposing team featured a boy. That team? Somerset Berkley. To be fair, the Massachusetts Interscholastic Athletic Association has tried to provide boys with a league of their own. In 2021, it voted to establish a seven-on-seven boys' field hockey league, but there simply weren't enough boys interested in playing to make it viable. That's unfortunate for the boys who love the sport. But why should the girls bear the competitive consequences of field hockey's lack of popularity among males? Which brings us to coach Crook herself. Yes, her sons love field hockey and haven't had the opportunity to compete with boys at the high school level. But does that mean she should have encouraged them to compete against girls? Saturday, after her son's final high school game, Crook addressed the controversy with reporters. "Is it that bad that I was a stay-at-home mother and I taught my son how to play field hockey? I got sick of playing wiffle ball, so I gave him a stick and I taught him how to play. And now the state of Massachusetts hates me," she said. "That's how I feel." Nobody is taking issue with Crook teaching her sons how to play field hockey. That's not the decision being questioned. The criticism from women's sports advocates such as Riley Gaines and Jennifer Sey centers on the competitive advantages males bring to female sports — regardless of how those males identify. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE But Monday, an Outsports writer offered a different interpretation of their criticism. "Anti-trans activists like Jennifer Sey and Riley Gaines have jumped into the athlete-bashing, seemingly equating this cis boy participating with trans girls." PABLO TORRE SAYS NCAA HAS NO TRANSGENDER ATHLETES, CONVENIENTLY LEAVES OUT THE REASON WHY The writer offered no explanation as to what made their criticism anti-trans. In fact, in a social media post addressing this very situation, Gaines wrote, "Girls deserve fair play, safety, and equal opportunity." Notice she didn't say anything about the boy's gender identity. That's because her stated concern is competitive fairness, not how the athlete identifies. In the end, this story illustrates two things: males have an unmistakable biological advantage, and the people speaking out don't care whether those males are trans. They'd just like you to know that another boy helped take a title from girls. The thing that never happens just keeps on happening. articles.title: Records tumble as Indian teen Sooryavanshi smashes 53-ball 204 against UAE
articles.summary: The 15-year-old Sooryavanshi struck a staggering 28 sixes, the most ever in a senior men’s innings.
articles.body:
Teenage sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi hammered 204 off 53 balls for India A to break a host of records, including for both the fastest century and double-century in List A cricket.

The 15-year-old Sooryavanshi struck a staggering 28 sixes, the most ever in a senior men’s innings, as India passed their target of 250 against the United Arab Emirates on Tuesday in just 14.2 overs.

Sooryavanshi reached his hundred off 28 balls to take Australian Jake Fraser-McGurk’s record by one delivery.

He raised his 200 off 52 deliveries, smashing the 103-ball mark previously held by Chad Bowes.

Sooryavanshi also broke his own record for fastest 150, reaching that milestone from 40 balls.

“No words to say for him. I would only say it’s like absolute carnage,” India A captain Tilak Varma said after the Asia Cup Rising Stars match.

“The way he played, I think first five overs, the match was done. Five overs, we are 100, and the way he carried on after that, it was tremendous to watch. Honestly, everyone knows how he can hit the sixes.”

In July, Sooryavanshi became India’s youngest men’s international when he made his T20I debut against England in Manchester, eclipsing Sachin Tendulkar’s longstanding record.

He amassed 776 runs for Rajasthan Royals to finish as the tournament’s leading run-scorer in this year’s IPL, at a remarkable strike rate of 237.30.

articles.title: Dylan Larkin Reacts to Canadiens Debut After Trade from Red Wings, Forfeiting $1M in Salary
articles.summary: The Montreal Canadiens came up short in a 2-1 loss to the Los Angeles Kings on Monday, but Dylan Larkin's performance in his debut offered plenty of encouragement.
articles.body:
The Montreal Canadiens came up short in a 2-1 loss to the Los Angeles Kings on Monday, but Dylan Larkin's performance in his debut offered plenty of encouragement.

Larkin assisted on Alex Newhook's goal in the second period. He called the night "incredible."

"I'm so grateful for that welcome, and to feel it on the ice and to feel it in the room with the guys right from when I got the call last night, it's a pretty special group in here and a lot of really good people around the organization," he told reporters . "And then to step out there and put the jersey on it's nothing I've experienced in my career. It's a very emotional night for me."

Coach Martin St. Louis was likewise positive with his assessment of Larkin.

"I liked his game," he said. "He's in control of both ends of the ice when he's out there. I liked his pace and his engagement. The way we play is similar, maybe not in everything but it's not like it's completely the opposite of what he's used to."

The Canadiens ended Larkin's long stalemate with the Detroit Red Wings on Sunday, acquiring him in a deal that included Michael Hage, Kirby Dach, Samuel Montembeault and draft compensation.

The Michigan native wasn't afraid to make things messy with his hometown team. His refusal to suit up cost him a little more than $1 million in forfeited salary.

Larkin clearly grew tired of the Red Wings' futility. Their playoff drought could stretch to 11 years this season.

The Canadiens, on the other hand, are coming off a conference finals appearance. During Monday's introductory press conference, general manager Kent Hughes said he's confident the franchise will give Larkin every reason to want to stick around:

The Colorado Avalanche are ahead for the Canadiens on Wednesday and a matchup with the Vegas Golden Knights follows that on Saturday. Both games should be tricky encounters for Montreal, but beating a pair of fellow playoff contenders would give the team plenty of momentum to fully kick off the Larkin era.

articles.summary: Charlotte Flair has had her own fair share of struggles despite being one of the greatest female WWE superstars of all time.
articles.body: Charlotte Flair has had her own fair share of struggles despite being one of the greatest female WWE superstars of all time. The Queen went through three failed marriages, the last of which was to former WWE star Andrade. Flair faced a lot of problems during the struggles of her marriage, which even led her to question herself as a person.Charlotte Flair admits she had begun to doubt herself during problems with former WWE star AndradeIn a recent interview with Insight with Chris Van Vliet, Charlotte Flair admitted that she constantly began to blame herself for the problems in her marriage. This led Ric Flair’s daughter to even question the fact that whether she was unattractive or if her highly successful WWE career over Andrade became the issue.The 14-time WWE Women’s Champion said, “I took the problems in the marriage as, like, I must not be pretty enough. Why are these things happening? ‘Cause I’m not pretty enough? Or are these happening because my career is here and his is here? Like, things that I could—like, not my fault.”Charlotte Flair had hid about her divorceCharlotte Flair and Andrade’s two-year marriage came to an end in 2024, and their divorce was finalized in October 2025. However, she tried hard to keep it a secret from the public eye as she was embarrassed about being divorced for the third time. “I think a lot of women stay in marriages because they don’t want to be embarrassed. I was mortified. That’s why I didn’t tell anyone when I came back”, said Flair.Charlotte Flair suspected her ex-husband had leaked the news about her divorceDespite her best efforts to keep the news under wraps, it eventually came out after Charlotte Flair returned to WWE after her year-long knee injury and won the 2025 Women’s Royal Rumble match. This led The Queen to suspect that it was Andrade himself who had leaked the news. She said, “When I won Rumble, and then it was on Raw, and then all of a sudden it hits the headlines, I was like, oh, I bet he did that just to embarrass me.”Despite that, Charlotte Flair has moved on in her life and is still hoping to have a family and marriage one day. articles.title: TOISA 2026: Meet the nominees for Equestrian
articles.summary: Discover the top contenders for the Equestrian category at the TOISA 2026, including remarkable achievements from Sresht Raju, Hriday Chheda, and Shruti Vora, at this prestigious celebration of Indian sports.
articles.body: The Times of India Sports Awards (TOISA) will return for its ninth edition on December 6, 2026, with Dehradun, Uttarakhand, set to host the annual celebration of Indian sporting excellence.The awards will recognise outstanding performances across disciplines during a year that featured two major multi-sport events - the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow and the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya - alongside world championships and other international competitions.The nominees for Equestrian reflect the breadth of Indian equestrian in 2026. Across the season, the shortlisted athletes and teams featured in major events, national and international competitions, and important milestones in their respective disciplines. The shortlist includes Sresht Raju, Hriday Chheda and Shruti Vora, among the contenders whose performances will be recognised at this year's awards.Meet the nominees for the TOISA 2026 Equestrian award.Sresht RajuAge: 15Key Achievements in 2026:- Won team jumping gold with Team Asia at the Dakar Youth Olympic Games.- Delivered a double-clear performance in the team competition.- Finished seventh in the individual event after reaching the 12-rider jump-off.- Won Big Tour gold at the Surge Equestrian League in April, riding Dancing Queen.Fifteen-year-old Sresht Raju Mantena enjoyed a breakthrough 2026 season, headlined by a team jumping gold medal at the Dakar Youth Olympic Games in November. Competing on an unfamiliar, lottery-drawn horse, Crazy Horse Boop, he delivered a standout performance to help Team Asia secure the title. He also impressed in the individual event, reaching the 12-rider jump-off before finishing seventh. His international success followed strong domestic form, including a Big Tour gold at the Surge Equestrian League in April.Hriday ChhedaAge: 28Key Achievements in 2026:- Finished eighth in the individual dressage final at the Asian Games with 72.680%.- Qualified for the individual final with an 11th-place finish in the combined standings.- Helped India secure fourth place in team dressage, scoring 67.353%.Indian dressage rider Hriday Chheda enjoyed a good 2026 season, finishing eighth in the individual dressage final at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games - the best result by an Indian equestrian at the event. Riding 19-year-old Dono Di Maggio, he progressed through both qualification rounds to reach the medal contest, where he scored 72.680%. He also helped India finish fourth in the team event, narrowly missing a podium place. His campaign was particularly significant after his individual final disqualification at the 2023 Asian Games, making his top-eight finish a personal milestone.Shruti VoraAge: 55Key Achievements in 2026:- Won silver in Intermediate I Freestyle at Hickstead CDI1 with 74.400%.- Secured bronze in Intermediate I at Wellington CDI1 with 70.931%.- Posted India's highest score of 68.059% in the Asian Games team dressage event.- Helped India finish fourth in team dressage at the Asian Games.Veteran Indian dressage rider Shruti Vora delivered a strong season on the international circuit, highlighted by podium finishes at CDI1 events in Great Britain and a leading contribution to India's Asian Games campaign. Riding Magnanimous, the 55-year-old finished runner-up in the Intermediate I Freestyle at Hickstead with 74.400% and secured third place in the Intermediate I at Wellington with 70.931%. At the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games, she recorded India's highest score of 68.059% in the team dressage event, helping the country finish fourth. She also placed ninth in the opening individual qualification round but missed the final after finishing 24th in the second qualifier.Ashish LimayeAge: 32Key Achievements in 2026:- Won gold in CCI2-L* at Montelibretti aboard Easy Turn.- Secured bronze in CCI2-S* at Montelibretti riding Willy Be Dun.- Finished 12th individually at the Asian Games, India's best result in eventing.- Became the third Indian to compete at the FEI World Eventing Championships, finishing 58th in Aachen.Indian eventing rider Ashish Limaye enjoyed a landmark 2026 season, becoming only the third Indian to compete at the FEI World Eventing Championships in Aachen, where he finished 58th. He also secured a 12th-place individual finish at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games, the best among India's eventers. Limaye began the season with two podium finishes at Montelibretti, Italy, winning CCI2-L gold and CCI2-S bronze. His campaign showcased his ability to compete across international events and major championships.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

The shortlist includes Rudrankksh Patil, Himanshu Dhillon and Kamaljeet Sahlot, among the contenders whose performances will be recognised at this year's awards.Meet the nominees for the TOISA 2026 Shooter of the Year (Male) award.Rudrankksh PatilAge: 22Key Achievements in 2026:- Won individual gold in men's 10m air rifle at the 2026 Asian Rifle and Pistol Championships in New Delhi.- Won team gold in men's 10m air rifle alongside Arjun Babuta and Vishal Singh at the Asian Championships.- Won individual bronze in men's 10m air rifle at the 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya.- Won team silver in men's 10m air rifle at the Asian Games.- Won another team silver in men's 50m rifle 3 positions at the Asian Games.Rudrankksh Patil enjoyed a productive 2026 season, winning two gold medals at the Asian Rifle and Pistol Championships in New Delhi before adding three podium finishes at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games. The Thane-born shooter claimed individual gold in the men's 10m air rifle event at the continental championships, following it up with another gold in the team event alongside Arjun Babuta and Vishal Singh.He continued his medal-winning run at the Asian Games, securing an individual bronze in the men's 10m air rifle event and contributing to India's silver-medal finishes in the men's 10m air rifle team and men's 50m rifle 3 positions team events. His three-medal haul made him one of India's most successful shooters at the Games.Born on December 16, 2003, in Thane, Maharashtra, Patil initially explored several sports, including chess, football, swimming and badminton, before taking up shooting. He announced himself on the international stage in 2022, winning the men's 10m air rifle world championship title in Cairo at just 18, and has since established himself among India's leading rifle shooters.Himanshu DhillonAge: 21Key Achievements in 2026:- Won individual silver in the 10m air rifle at the 2026 Asian Games.- Won team silver in the 10m air rifle at the Asian Games.- Won bronze in the 10m air rifle mixed team event with Sonam Maskar at the ISSF World Cup in Hangzhou.- Won gold in the 10m air rifle mixed team event at the 68th National Shooting Championship Competitions.Himanshu Dhillon enjoyed a breakthrough 2026 season, winning two silver medals at the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya. The shooter from Jind, Haryana, finished second in the individual 10m air rifle event and also helped India win silver in the team event.Dhillon also made his mark at the international level by winning his first senior-level medal in July 2026. He partnered Sonam Maskar to win bronze in the 10m air rifle mixed team event at the ISSF World Cup in Hangzhou. He later added another major achievement by winning gold in the 10m air rifle mixed team event at the 68th National Shooting Championship Competitions.Dhillon initially started as a wrestler. However, after trying shooting for a few weeks, he decided to continue with the sport following a coach's suggestion.Kamaljeet SahlotAge: 23Key Achievements in 2026:- Won mixed team pistol gold at the 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya.- Broke the Asian Games record in the mixed team pistol final.- Won team gold at the 2026 Asian Championships in New Delhi.- Won individual silver at the Asian Championships.Kamaljeet Sahlot had an impressive 2026 season, winning gold at the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya and adding two more medals at the Asian Championships in New Delhi. Competing in the 10m air pistol and 50m pistol events, Sahlot won the mixed team pistol gold at the Asian Games. He also set a new Asian Games record during the final of the event.At the 2026 Asian Championships in New Delhi, Sahlot continued his strong run, winning gold in the team event and silver in the individual competition. The shooter from Rewari, Haryana, established himself as one of India's notable performers in pistol shooting during the year.Kynan ChenaiAge: 35Key Achievements in 2026:- Won mixed team trap gold at the 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya alongside Neeru Dhanda.- Scored 34 targets in the final to beat Qatar (32) and China (23).- Finished fourth in qualification with 136 targets alongside Dhanda.Kynan Chenai enjoyed a successful 2026 season, winning mixed team trap gold alongside Neeru Dhanda at the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya. The Indian pair scored 34 targets in the final to beat Qatar (32) and China (23). They had qualified fourth for the final with a score of 136. Shooting runs in the family for Chenai. His father, Darius Chenai, is a former national shooting champion and initially coached him when he took up the sport in 2003. He later trained under four-time Olympian Mansher Singh. Interestingly, shooting was not the only sport Chenai excelled in during his school days. articles.title: Three-point attack lifts Michigan Women’s Basketball to victory over Miami
articles.summary: In an early battle of undefeated teams, No. 2 Michigan Women’s Basketball outshot Miami from beyond the arc and won by more than 20 points in the Bahamas:
articles.body:
The No. 2 Michigan women's basketball team faced its second power conference opponent of the season, facing Miami in the Bahamas at the Baha Mar Pink Flamingo Championship. The Hurricanes, coming off a WBIT appearance and riding an undefeated start, provided a new measuring stick for the Wolverines after two blowout wins .

Michigan (6-0) soundly defeated Miami (6-1), handing the Hurricanes their first loss of the season, 79-58, behind a downpour of threes. Led by junior guard Syla Swords' 18 points on 6-for-10 shooting beyond the arc, the Wolverines buried 11 triples — including a 71.4 percent first-quarter clip — to separate.

Head coach Kim Barnes Arico has long professed the benefits of "trading threes for twos," defeating opponents by sinking more long-range shots while surrendering more points in the paint. While the Hurricanes outscored the Wolverines 34-24 in the paint, Michigan outpaced Miami beyond the arc. Shooting 11-for-25 to the Hurricanes' 3-for-15, the Wolverines' altogether lower 45 percent shooting clip from the floor still served as a key separator.

Swords and Michigan began the game solely succeeding from beyond the arc, with Swords shooting a perfect 3-for-3 in the first quarter and the Wolverines strangely missing each of their 10 first-quarter two-point attempts. Miami's defensive focus was to make Michigan beat them from beyond the arc, and Swords took on the challenge.

"We did a good job at the beginning of finding (Swords)," junior guard Olivia Olson told The Michigan Daily . "She shot really well today. She always does, but she really showed that today. We played into their scheme of letting us settle for threes."

The Wolverines' 50 percent first-half clip from range, good for nine threes, established a lead strong enough to withstand the Hurricanes' surges. Michigan built its 19-16 first-quarter lead on the back of Swords' catch-and-shoot success and a 4-for-4 start from the free throw line. Miami's interior defensive focus meant the Wolverines had to screen Swords open to get clean looks or find her in transition, which they did to a tune of five first-half threes.

Early on, Miami got going inside the arc, led by guard Gal Raviv's perfect 3-for-3 start and eight points. Raviv led the Hurricanes and all scorers with 25 points, taking them the hard way with tough midrange jumpers.

Miami's defense picked up in the second quarter, holding the Wolverines scoreless in the final 4:09 amid a 7-0 run that cut the margin to 41-32 at halftime. Still, Michigan had poked enough holes in the Hurricanes' defense for the three-point downpour to leak through.

Each quarter, the Wolverines piled on to their lead, extending it one surge at a time. Despite junior forward Kendall Dudley and senior forward Ashley Sofilkanich sitting for long stretches due to foul trouble, Michigan's defense disrupted the Hurricanes' path and generated frequent turnovers. Jumping passing lanes and running in transition, the Wolverines forced 21 turnovers — including 10 steals — and scored 23 points off them.

"Our goal is always to try to speed people up, and our pressure is able to do that," Barnes Arico told The Michigan Daily . "We didn't want to sit in the halfcourt and have to defend Miami's offense, so (the press) gave us an opportunity to pick them up."

Miami gave Michigan a different halfcourt matchup than the Wolverines have faced so far this season. Led by 5-foot-9 Raviv's distributions, the rest of the Hurricanes imposed a height disadvantage and capitalized in the paint early. Michigan entered the game with the goal of turning Miami over or picking up in the full court to disrupt Miami's rhythm.

Despite the Hurricanes' height mismatch, Michigan's guards stepped up and slowed down Miami enough in the paint to let its own offense reinforce the lead. Matching junior guard Olivia Olson as the Wolverines' leading scorer, junior guard Te'Yala Delfosse scored 12 of her 19 points in the fourth quarter to seal the game.

articles.title: 4 downs: Raiders valiant comeback bid falls short in Denver
articles.summary: Raiders rally from 17-point deficit but fall short against Broncos in 38-24 loss. We go four downs for some key observations.
articles.body:
In Sunday's matchup against the Denver Broncos , the Las Vegas Raiders fell behind 17-0 but battled back to tie it at 17 in the third quarter. Denver later went up 31-24, and the Raiders had a chance to tie, but Fernando Mendoza threw a costly pick-six that put the Broncos up 38-24, the final score. The Raiders are now 4-7.

First down: Fernando Mendoza showed he can play in the NFL

It was Mendoza's second career start and first road start on Sunday against a tough Broncos defense. He threw three touchdown passes: the first came on a 68-yard pass to Ashton Jeanty, then Ian Thomas on a play-action pass for 19 yards, then Jack Bech from seven yards out.

Mendoza finished the game completing 18-of-37 passes for 267 yards, three touchdowns, and one interception. He also rushed for 22 yards, but took five sacks.

It was nice to see Mendoza push the ball downfield, and I would like to see him try to get out of the pocket more instead of taking sacks. This is something that has to happen going forward.

The Raiders and Raiders fans have been waiting for Jack Bech to start producing. On Sunday, with Brock Bowers out with an ankle injury, Bech answered the call with eight catches for 88 yards and touchdowns -- both career highs.

During the comeback, Bech had a couple of key third-down catches, and it looked like he and Mendoza had good chemistry together. The Raiders need receivers to step up; hopefully Bech is ready to turn the corner and become the consistent receiver they need. He now has 16 catches for 155 yards and two touchdowns on the season.

Third down: Ashton Jeanty finally gets going

Las Vegas has struggled to run the ball all season; on Sunday, behind Jeanty, the Raiders' running game opened up some. The second-year running back rushed for 79 yards on 11 carries, including a 46-yard run that set up a field goal. Las Vegas rushed for 143 yards, with Mike Washington Jr. adding 42. It was the first time the Raiders have rushed for 100 yards since Week 3.

The Raiders got back into the game, so they kept running the ball, and the offensive line did a good job creating push for the running backs to have success.

Also, Jeanty added five catches for 90 yards and one touchdown, for 169 yards from scrimmage. He had a good game for the Raiders but touched the ball only four times in the second half, which was mind boggling.

Hopefully Sunday's game can get Jeanty going for the rest of the season; the Raiders will need him to take some of the pressure off Mendoza.

The run defense is still a huge problem for the team. Against Denver, the Raiders gave up 133 yards, with Jonah Coleman picking up 111 yards and three touchdowns on 24 carries (4.6 yards per carry).

Denver's offensive line was getting push on the interior of the Raiders' defensive line all game long. It's hard to stop the run when your defensive tackles can't eat up space and blocks. That's why Las Vegas is 31st in rush defense, giving up 149.5 yards per game.

The Raiders had nine penalties for 63 yards, while the Broncos had two for 10 yards. Some of the Raiders' penalties were questionable, prompting Klint Kubiak to say at halftime, "They need to call it both ways."

One of the biggest penalties that hurt the Raiders was an offensive pass interference call on touchdown passes to Jalen Nailor. Receiver Cody White got called for the interference in the end zone and the Raiders were pushed back to the 14-yard line and had to settle for three.

articles.title: Organised Lazio Supporters Will Attend Atalanta Clash: “Protest Will Continue”
articles.summary: The organised Lazio fan groups will interrupt the stadium boycott to attend the team’s home fixture against Atalanta on December 6.The BackgroundThe Curva No...
articles.body:
The organised Lazio fan groups will interrupt the stadium boycott to attend the team's home fixture against Atalanta on December 6.

The Curva Nord Ultras and other sections of the fanbase have been protesting against unpopular Lazio president Claudio Lotito by vacating their seats during the team's home games as a means to deprive the patron of matchday revenue and force him to sell the club, or at least apologise for his treatment of the supporters throughout his time at the club. They have only been attending away games.

Lazio fans (Photo by Emmanuele Ciancaglini/Getty Images)

However, Lotito remains stubborn in his stance, refusing to entertain the possibility of a sale. He also believes the team's current status as the shock leaders of the Serie A table has vindicated his work.

Organised Lazio Supporters Will Be Back Against Atalanta

While the tug-of-war between the owner and the fanbase is showing no signs of ending any time soon, an interesting development occurred on Tuesday, as the Lazio fan groups have announced they will be in attendance when Lazio host Atalanta on December 6.

The organised supporters released a new statement (via La Lazio Siamo Noi ), berating Lotito and the club's top officials, accusing them of supporting their arch-rivals Roma.

In December, we have decided to give ourselves an entire month of Lazio. A year ago, this would have been the norm for the Biancocelesti faithful. Unfortunately, however, a tyrannical president and his large group of Roma-supporting followers have forced us into that extreme act of love which has taken us away from our own home.During these long months of absence, we have realised that this protest enjoys very solid support, as it has continued to have an entire fanbase behind it, having freely chosen to support it.By contrast, the people at the top of this club have done absolutely nothing to bring the supporters closer again. Instead, they have continued moving in precisely the opposite direction, while the Lazio faithful have continued to choose which side they stand on.

Lazio Fans Pay Respect to Gennaro Gattuso

On the other hand, the Lazio fan groups lauded Lazio head coach Gennaro Gattuso for showing empathy towards their movement, identifying him as one of the reasons behind their decision to make a one-off appearance against Atalanta.

There have been very few exceptions. Among them, there are certainly Mister Gattuso, who has repeatedly reiterated that he understands and accepts our decision, while expressing his 'dream' of seeing the Stadio Olimpico packed with his own people, and his team (shaped in the manager's own image and likeness), who have come over to the away section after every away match to receive the applause they deserve. We know they are close to us!For him, for the team, but above all for all those children and supporters who have joined the protest by staying away from the stadium, those who were unable to purchase tickets for the derby, and all Lazio fans suffering from being separated from their beloved Lazio, we have decided to pay tribute to them by attending the Lazio-Atalanta match on December 6.

The fan groups had already revealed their intention to attend both clashes against Roma since the start of the season. Hence, they believe that attending the Atalanta game could serve as a timely warm-up for the first edition of the Derby della Capitale, which will take place on December 13.

We will also fire the players up ahead of the derby, giving them a taste of the atmosphere they will experience on December 13 and demonstrating that we are always by their side because they deserve it!In previous years, we went to Formello to cheer them on, but we no longer consider that training ground 'our home'. Several friendly matches were played there, and Mr Lotito thought it best to hold them behind closed doors out of fear of protests. He locked the team inside a bunker, showing complete disregard for all those supporters who would have liked to watch and encourage the players who are now giving us so much satisfaction.

Lazio Stadium Boycott to Resume in January

Finally, the statement insisted this won't be the end of the stadium boycott, which will be resumed after the Christmas holiday.

This does not mean putting an end to the protest, which will continue inside the stadium for this particular match, nor should anyone mistakenly believe that we are returning permanently. It is simply yet another demonstration of the unity and solidarity of a fanbase standing together against a despot.The protest will continue under the same arrangements established at the beginning of the year. We will continue attending away matches and derbies only. Then, if and when we all want to, we may choose another day to celebrate our Lazio identity.This is not a step backwards. Others are the ones who must take a step forward, starting with the Roma supporter occupying the position of communications director (how will he behave at the derby? Will he cheer with his heart, or will he continue thinking about his wallet?).We remain firm in our position, which has not changed in the slightest and is not influenced by our excellent start to the season or our deserved position in the league table.Our completely negative assessment of Mr Lotito's behaviour and the shameful, amateurish management of the capital's leading club only strengthen our conviction that change is urgently needed. The club must keep pace with a football world moving at three times the speed of Lazio. Such change is also owed to a fanbase that lives and breathes this immense love every day, yet finds itself forced to endure a nightmare characterised by incompetence and strokes of luck.As we already said when we decided against purchasing season tickets and chose to follow Lazio only away from home, anyone who wishes to remain outside is free to do so. Those who want to join us should get ready to experience 90 minutes of pure love!Bring your children, put a flag in their hands and a scarf around their necks, and tell them that, for Christmas, we are giving ourselves a December full of Lazio, with four matches that will recharge our batteries until the return derby!FORZA LAZIO! FORZA LAZIALI!"

articles.title: Press Taylor discusses what's wrong with Bears run game
articles.summary: The Bears offense has a big problem with their ailing run game. Press Taylor sounded off on those struggles.
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears offense had another lackluster showing in Sunday's 21-13 win over the New Orleans Saints . But perhaps the most disappointing aspect of the offense was once again the run game, which has been declining since a strong start to the 2026 season.

There was hope that the return of Kyle Monangai would provide a spark for the run game, but that wasn't the case. While Chicago totaled 146 rushing yards against New Orleans, only 102 of those came from running backs with D'Andre Swift, Monangai and Salvon Ahmed. As for what's the cure to the ailing run game, offensive coordinator Press Taylor admitted that it isn't just one thing that would serve as a magic fix-it.

"Yeah, I think it's kind of an everything issue," Taylor said. "I think there's a lot of things that we as a coaching staff feel like we can detail things up even a little bit better putting guys in the best possible position from execution from the little fundamentals to a variety of looks that we provide throughout our practice. There's just a number of issues that we feel like we can do a better job of, and so we're working to get that corrected."

Bears beat Saints, 21-13: Photos from Chicago's Week 11 win

It's been a tale of two quarters for the Bears run game. In Weeks 1-4, the Bears averaged 196 rushing yards per game eclipsing 230 yards twice and hitting 120-plus in each game. In Weeks 5-8, Chicago averaged just 105 yards per game, falling short of 100 yards in two games before bouncing back with 116, 126 and 146 yards in their last four games.

The Bears offense has gone from explosive to underwhelming, and the run game struggles are a key reason why. Chicago relies on the run to open up play action and establish a balanced attack that helps them dominate time of possession, which there's no better team at accomplishing this season.

Last year, the bye week provided an opportunity to fix a struggling run game. While it's only been one game, it hasn't been an immediate fix heading into the most difficult remaining schedule in the final seven weeks.

articles.title: Senegal reinstated as 2025 Africa Cup of Nations winners over Morocco
articles.summary: Court of Arbitration for Sport rules in Senegal’s favour over the controversial final in January.
articles.body:
Senegal have been reinstated as 2025 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) winners ⁠⁠after the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) upheld ‌‌their appeal against being stripped of the title.

The Moroccans will lose the title that was controversially awarded to them by the Confederation of African Football (CAF) two months after the chaotic final on January 18 in Rabat , where Senegal emerged 1-0 winners.

CAS’s ruling follows an appeal by Senegal after they were stripped of the title in March by African football’s governing body.

CAF had declared that Senegal forfeited the match when players walked off the pitch in protest at a penalty awarded to Morocco. The Senegal team returned after 14 minutes and scored in extra time.

The CAS panel, presided over by French sports law expert Gerald Simon with assistance from Italian international law professor Luigi ‌‌Fumagalli and Ulrich Haas, a Hamburg-based lawyer and professor of law at the University of Zurich, found that “the ‌‌referee ‌‌did not commit any error of law”, said CAS secretary general Matthieu Reeb.

Senegal, who celebrated the trophy win with fanfare on their return home in January, were incensed by the penalty decision and lodged an appeal at CAS, the highest court for sports-related disputes.

Announcing its “crusade” against CAF’s ruling, Senegal’s football governing body then claimed the move could “reshape the world of football” ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠and undermine the principle that refereeing decisions are final.

“This decision cannot even be considered a true sporting justice ruling – it is so crude, so absurd, so irrational,” lawyer Juan de Dios Crespo Perez, representing Senegal’s governing body, had said.

What was the Senegal-Morocco AFCON final controversy?

Senegal were enraged after a late penalty was awarded to Morocco in the second half. The players left the pitch in protest as Congolese referee Jean-Jacques Ndala awarded the spot kick, following a VAR review of a challenge on Morocco forward Brahim Diaz by El Hadji Malick Diouf.

The Senegalese had already protested to the referee in the second minute of stoppage time about an Ibrahim Sarr goal which was ruled out for a foul.

Before Diaz could take the penalty, the Senegalese players and coaching staff left the field, with many believing the game might well end there.

Senegal eventually returned and Diaz missed the spot kick before the match headed to extra time, when Pape Gueye’s stunning strike settled the game 1-0 in favour of the Teranga Lions.

Senegal were ruled to ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠have forfeited the final after walking off the pitch, led by coach Pape Thiaw, in protest at the potentially decisive penalty awarded to Morocco.

When play resumed after a delay of about 15 minutes, Morocco forward Brahim Diaz’s penalty was saved. In extra time, Pape Gueye scored the decisive goal that saw Senegal become champions of Africa for the second time.

Less than two months later, CAF ruled Senegal to have forfeited the match by walking off and officially recorded the result as a 3-0 win for Morocco.

articles.title: “We Need Great Resourcing”: Jon Sumrall Makes Open Plea to Florida’s Hierarchy as He Demands Funds to Improve Results
articles.summary: Florida has managed a decent 7-4 record this season, and head coach Jon Sumrall wants the program to take a step in the right direction so that next season c...
articles.body:
Florida has managed a decent 7-4 record this season, and head coach Jon Sumrall wants the program to take a step in the right direction so that next season can be even better.

Speaking to reporters about the program's future, Sumrall made it clear he needs more funds to invest in the squad, highlighting the importance of spending money the right way to take Florida back to the top.

"We need great resourcing," Sumrall said in a direct message to the Florida hierarchy and boosters.

"I'm not going to shy away from the fact that if you have championship expectations, you need to have championship resourcing…there's a lot of good here. Can we make it better? Yeah, we can make it better."

Sumrall further said that proper resourcing would help Florida beat ranked teams all the time, rather than just hoping they can beat the big guns.

"Let's put ourselves in the group where we don't hope we can win, we should win – or you should run me out of here," he said.

Jon Sumrall Spoke About the Importance of Beating Florida State in Recruiting

Fans often judge head coaches from their performances against their closest rivals, and this week Florida faces bitter rivals Florida State, and Jon Sumrall wants to beat the Seminoles both on and off the field.

"It's a big deal," Sumrall said about beating Florida State both in recruiting and on the field, as per Gators Wire .

"You have a lot of respect for everybody we play in the state, or even the ones we don't, but you want to win the in-state battles, whether it's on the field, in recruiting or whatever. We compete every day, so it's a huge deal."

He also shared a message from former Florida coach Urban Meyer while discussing the impact of a game that has garnered major attention from across the state over the years.

"Coach Meyer texted me, gosh, maybe around the Texas game. He just said, 'Hey, finish this thing strong all the way down the stretch of November. Recruit the roster you need to recruit to build this thing.'

"This game is a big part of it. In-state rivalries matter. Anybody who says it's just another game, I don't buy into that. It's not just another game. It's an in-state rivalry. Those are different."

Florida and Florida State lock horns in a massive clash on Friday in Tallahassee.

articles.title: Maui Invitational: Top 25 BYU on upset alert against red hot Ole Miss
articles.summary: The Cougars could be without its leading scorer while the Rebels played some of its best basketball on Monday
articles.body:
The Maui Invitational semi-finals are here, and Ole Miss will play No. 19 BYU on Tuesday for a chance to play for the tournament championship on Wednesday.

The Rebels (5-0) and Cougars (6-0) should be some must watch basketball if you're "working from home" or just outright streaming games from your office during Thanksgiving week. These two teams had very different first games in Maui with BYU needing a come back to topple Washington, 83-77.

Ole Miss meanwhile demolished Clemson by 20 points in a game that seemed over in the first few minutes. The Rebels have played with a defensive intensity this season that pays off scoring more than 20 points off turnovers in every game thus far.

BYU should bring the toughest competition to date for Chris Beard and his squad. Washington played a pretty flawless first half on Monday leading the Cougars 39-31, but BYU exploded for 52 points in the second half.

The comeback centered around rebounding and flat out better shooting, so the overall effort on the court today has to be a very high level. BYU lost the turnover battle with Washington, and it had below average free throw percentage (22/36, 61 percent) but still found a way to win.

The matchup challenge will be with BYU guard Collin Chandler who stands at 6'6" and scored 24 points on Monday. The Rebels will have to rely on 6'5" Ilias Kamardine or Patton Pinkins to pick Chandler up and shut him down. The Cougars have played its last two games without leading scorer Robert Wright III (24.3 ppg) who was listed day to day with muscle tightness, but the program hoped to have him back this week.

There's no hiding or flying under the radar now for Ole Miss who the college basketball world were unaware of until yesterday. An upset on Tuesday would only build its resume in non-conference play and bring one of the best wins to Ole Miss since the 2024-2025 season.

Ole Miss and BYU tipoff at 1:30 p.m. CT, and it will be broadcast live on ESPN2 from the Lahaina Community Center in Maui.

articles.title: Mets Reportedly Interested In 3.23 ERA Starting Pitcher After Signing Tarik Skubal
articles.summary: The New York Mets may be looking to add another starting pitcher
articles.body:
The New York Mets have already landed their ace by signing Tarik Skubal to a nine-year, $450 million deal.

However, they may not feel satisfied with their rotation just yet. Behind Skubal, the Mets have Nolan McLean, Zac Thornton, Christian Scott, Sean Manaea, Kodai Senga and Jonah Tong. McLean, Thornton, and Scott could be solid, but Manaea, Senga, and Tong come with a ton of questions.

There are still quality starters on the open market, and the Mets are reportedly interested in Michael King.

"Sources: Mets would still like to add another starter and one they've shown interest in is Michael King," wrote Mets insider Mike Mayer on X on Monday.

King is expected to sign one of the more expensive deals on the open market right now. After signing Skubal, many expected the Mets to target cheaper free agents. However, Steve Cohen may feel a need to improve his rotation as much as possible.

King has a 3.23 career ERA and has been great for the San Diego Padres in the last three seasons. Since joining the Padres and becoming a full-time starter, King has a 3.15 ERA. He was phenomenal in the postseason this year and deserves to be paid like a top-tier starter.

With whispers of a lockout and a salary cap, the Mets dropping a bag on King would be a surprise.

articles.title: Coen evaluates play of Jessie Bates, Jordan Davis in Jaguars debuts
articles.summary: After reviewing the tape, head coach Liam Coen shared what he saw from Jessie Bates and Jordan Davis in their Jaguars debuts.
articles.body:
Jordan Davis and Jessie Bates made their Jacksonville Jaguars debuts on Sunday against the New York Giants . After reviewing the tape, head coach Liam Coen shared what he saw from each player.

"I thought both guys did their jobs," Coen said on Monday. "Did well. I thought Jordan and Davon Godchaux did some really good things up front in terms of allowing our second-level guys to play freely. Our linebackers were free a lot in the run game. They disrupted some things."

Of the Jaguars ' 70 defensive snaps, Davis was on the field for 35 of them, according to PFF. Among the defensive tackles, only Arik Armstead (46) played more.

With his opportunities, Davis recorded two total tackles. However, as a stout interior presence, Davis' impact won't always show up on the stat sheet. But listed at 6-6 and weighing 336 pounds, Davis' ability to clog running lanes and eat up blocks can create opportunities for his teammates.

"Then I think Jessie just didn't have a ton of ops," Coen added. "Like there wasn't a lot of balls his way. He got kind of moved on the double move there that they ended up not hitting, but nothing really stood out in terms of glaring negatives."

There wasn't any easing in for Bates, who was on the field for 66 defensive snaps. The bulk of those reps came at deep safety, but he did see some snaps in the box and from the slot as well.

As a coverage defender, Bates was targeted only once and didn't allow a completion. He also made three total tackles, and generated a quarterback pressure as a blitzer.

"Fully anticipate those guys to be able to continue to help us and they're going to make some plays for our team," said Coen. "I don't doubt that whatsoever."

articles.title: RoWINg to Wisconsin - Opponent Preview
articles.summary: You know what week it is
articles.body:
The Minnesota Golden Gophers (6-5) will cross the border on Black Friday to close out the regular season against the Wisconsin Badgers (7-4) in their annual rivalry battle for Paul Bunyan's Axe.

Under second-year offensive coordinator Jeff Grimes, Wisconsin has pivoted away from the failed "Dairy Raid" offense to be more of a run-first offense with a physical, downhill ground game to set up the play-action pass. The results have not been great, as the Badgers rank 65th nationally in rushing offense, averaging 155.6 rushing yards per game. Iowa State transfer running back Abu Sama has been ineffective, averaging 20 rushing yards per game over the last four. Third-year running back Darrion Dupree has come on strong of late, racking up a combined 182 rushing yards and four touchdowns in the last two weeks.

Old Dominion transfer quarterback Colton Joseph is their leading rusher with 107 carries for 558 yards and six touchdowns. He has largely been ineffective as a passer in conference play. In six starts against Big Ten competition, Joseph has completed 51.6% of his passes and averaged 118 passing yards per game. But Grimes has utilized his legs and athleticism in designed runs, read-option plays, and RPOs to keep the offense ahead of the chains. The Minnesota defense will need to be disciplined against the run and tackle well in space to keep Joseph from getting into the open field and picking up easy yards.

He has also only been sacked nine times this season and has not thrown an interception since Week 4 against Penn State, so he has been able to limit negative plays that hurt the offense.

If the Badgers put the ball in the air, expect the target to be either fifth-year senior wide receiver Tyrell Henry or fourth-year senior tight end Jacob Harris. Henry is the team's leading receiver with 37 receptions for 439 receiving yards and a touchdown reception. He is an elusive slot receiver who can make plays after the catch. Harris is a rare blend of size, athleticism, and contested-catch reliability who can create matchup problems for defenses, especially in the red zone. He has a team-high four receiving touchdowns.

Please tell me the Gophers will be able to score

The Badgers rank 14th nationally in run defense (98.4 rushing yards allowed per game), 20th in pass defense (180.3 passing yards allowed per game), and 13th in scoring defense (16.5 points allowed per game).

This is a vintage Wisconsin defense. They are built to stop the run and generate pressure with blitzes, led by a group of linebackers that can read plays quickly, fill gaps aggressively, and make plays in the backfield. Sophomore linebackers Cooper Catalano and Mason Posa lead the way as the team's top two tacklers.

The name you need to know is Sebastian Cheeks. The fifth-year linebacker is a freak athlete and a runaway train off the edge, leading the Badgers with 10.5 tackles for loss and seven sacks.

If this Wisconsin defense has a weakness, it's in the secondary, where defensive coordinator Mike Tressel likes to plays zone coverage, which is unusual for a blitz-heavy defense. Opposing quarterbacks have frequently attacked their zone coverage with high-percentage throws, and when the Badgers have adjusted to man coverage, they've been vulnerable to quick RPO slant routes.

Fifth-year cornerback Javan Robinson has been their top cover corner, leading the team with seven pass breakups, but he got banged up two weeks ago in the loss to Maryland and missed last week's game against Purdue. Wisconsin also lost top safety Matt Jung to season-ending surgery earlier this month.

But who will score more points on Saturday?

Wisconsin is 5-0 at Camp Randall Stadium this season and Minnesota is 1-3 on the road, so I'd feel better about the Gophers' chances of retaining Paul Bunyan's Axe if this was a home game. But there's no way I'm picking the Badgers. Minnesota 17, Wisconsin 16.

articles.title: Dylan Larkin shares honest take on Montreal Canadiens fans after blockbuster trade
articles.summary: Larkin explains what makes the Bell Centre atmosphere special.
articles.body:
Dylan Larkin has already explained what makes playing at the Bell Centre different. The newly acquired Montreal Canadiens center believes the team's passionate supporters make the building special.

Larkin shared his thoughts during a recent morning skate after joining Montreal from the Detroit Red Wings. The 30-year-old NHL er also spoke about the franchise's history and his excitement about wearing its iconic crest.

" You notice it right away when you walk in . Such an iconic crest and the names that go along with it," Larkin said.

Montreal's history surrounds its players inside the facility. The 24 Stanley Cup championships appear through trophy displays, retired numbers, championship banners, and portraits of Hall of Fame players.

"I'm fortunate to be a part of it, to be honest with you," Larkin added. "I'm excited to hopefully get to know some of the legends and meet them and maybe get a picture or an autograph."

However, the Canadiens' supporters made an equally strong impression on him.

Dylan Larkin is eager to experience Bell Centre

"The Bell Centre, it's the fans," Larkin said, while praising the building's atmosphere. "They've nailed the acoustics, vibrations, and sight lines and everything that goes with a great building, but (it's also) the hockey knowledge the fans have, when to cheer, when not to cheer, when to be loud and when to sing that great (goal) song."

He said, "It's hard not to sing along when you're on the visiting team bench. I'm excited to be on the home bench."

That excitement reflects what Montreal gains beyond Larkin's production. His experience and leadership could help a young roster handle the pressure surrounding the franchise.

The Canadiens have a 14-7-4 record, sitting third in the Atlantic Division. Larkin gives Martin St. Louis another experienced center as Montreal pushes for a playoff position. His first appearance came against the Los Angeles Kings on Nov. 23. Larkin recorded an assist, although Montreal suffered a 2-1 defeat.

Speaking after his debut, he said, "It was a very emotional night for me."

He has also dismissed concerns about adjusting to his new surroundings.

"I think I'll be okay," Larkin said about finding the correct dressing room. "Everyone's been first-class here, pointing me in the right direction so far."

Montreal's supporters have already caught his attention. Now, Larkin must help give them more reasons to celebrate.

articles.title: Millwall punished with partial stadium closure over ‘ableist and homophobic chanting’
articles.summary: Millwall will have to close part of their stadium when they host Sheffield United next month
articles.body:
Millwall have been ordered to partially close their stadium after being found guilty of discriminatory chanting by supporters.

A regulatory commission proved two charges relating to disability and sexual orientation discrimination during January's fixture against Charlton. Consequently, the Sky Bet Championship team will host Sheffield United with a reduced capacity at The Den on 8 December.

Four blocks inside the Dockers Stand will be shut for the visit of the Blades.

The club have also been fined £70,000, issued an extended FA Action Plan, and handed another partial stadium closure, suspended until the end of next season.

A club statement read: "Both chants are discriminatory and offensive, and the club condemns them in the strongest possible terms.

"Ableist and homophobic chanting, as well as any other form of discriminatory chanting, has no place in football or society.

"Any individual identified as engaging in such abuse will face the consequences.

"The club will continue the significant work already achieved under its dedicated anti-discrimination campaign, 'All 'Wall', while continuously reviewing and enhancing best practice to ensure The Den is always a welcoming environment."

Last month, Millwall's match against Swansea was halted for seven minutes after an allegation of racist abuse from the crowd towards Swans substitute Eom Ji Sung was reported by the Welsh club to officials.

Referee Edward Duckworth halted the match in the 65th minute and walked to the dug-outs to speak with Lions boss Alex Neil, Swans counterpart Vitor Matos and fourth official Ruebyn Ricardo.

When play eventually resumed it was announced in the stadium that there had been a report of racist chanting, adding that police were working to identify any offenders using CCTV.

Millwall later released a statement on the incident which read: "Millwall Football Club is aware of an alleged, individual incident of discriminatory abuse towards a Swansea City player during the second-half of Tuesday evening's Sky Bet Championship match.

"The club operates a zero-tolerance policy towards any form of discriminatory abuse. Any individual found to have engaged in such behaviour will face the strongest possible action.

"The club is working alongside the relevant authorities to establish the facts and is unable to comment further as tonight's alleged incident is the subject of an ongoing police investigation, which the club fully supports."

articles.title: Why did CAS overturn AFCON final decision? Explaining court ruling to reinstate Senegal as African champions
articles.summary: After a long battle to protect the on-field result of the 2025 AFCON title match, Senegal have been reinstated as champions of Africa in a seismic decision b...
articles.body:
Senegal may have won the Africa Cup of Nations title all the way back in early 2026, but they have been fighting to protect their trophy through nearly the entirety of the calendar year.

Now, the Lions of Teranga have officially — and finally — retained their continental championship.

After defeating Morocco 1-0 in a controversial and contentious final on January 18, Senegal saw their title stripped in mid-March, with the African federation (CAF) reversing the result of the match and awarding Morocco the title based on a technicality.

Now, that decision itself has been overturned, and the result of the match reinstated, leaving Senegal with their second-ever AFCON championship.

CAS overturns AFCON final decision, reinstates Senegal as champions

On Tuesday, November 24, the Court of Arbitration for Sport handed down a seismic ruling that shifted the balance of power in African football once again.

CAS officially reinstated Senegal as AFCON 2025 champions, reversing the decision by the African federation (CAF) to disqualify the 1-0 final winners and hand Morocco the title by default.

Why did CAS name Senegal as AFCON champions?

The Court of Arbitration for Sport determined that Senegal were the rightful winners of the 2025 AFCON final, reinstating the final score of the match and overturning the CAF ruling that they should be disqualified.

According to the CAS decision, Senegal were deemed winners of the game because the tournament regulations were wrongly applied in favor of Morocco.

"AFCON Regulations are intended solely to determine the outcome of a match when a team's conduct leads the referee to call off the game permanently, they are therefore not applicable in this case," the CAS decision read. "After having examined the arguments raised by the Parties, the Arbitral Panel considered that the Referee's decision to resume the match or stop it fell definitively within his sole authority. By blowing his whistle to restart play, the Referee considered that the conditions for resuming the match had been met — both teams were on the pitch again, and both expressed their willingness to resume. "In the Panel's view, there is no doubt that the effects of the referee's decision were limited to the pitch. As such, the panel considers that the referee's decision was covered by the 'field of play' doctrine. "Since Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON Regulations are intended solely to determine the outcome of a match when a team's conduct leads the referee to call off the game permanently, they are therefore not applicable in this case. In conclusion, the panel considers that in resuming the match, the referee did not err in law." "The panel acknowledged that the referee had to make a decision in an atmosphere of extreme tension. However, these circumstances do not justify describing the decision as 'arbitrary.' On the contrary, the Referee's judgment did not appear to have been affected by factors external to the game."

"After having examined the arguments raised by the Parties, the Arbitral Panel considered that the Referee's decision to resume the match or stop it fell definitively within his sole authority. By blowing his whistle to restart play, the Referee considered that the conditions for resuming the match had been met — both teams were on the pitch again, and both expressed their willingness to resume.

"In the Panel's view, there is no doubt that the effects of the referee's decision were limited to the pitch. As such, the panel considers that the referee's decision was covered by the 'field of play' doctrine.

"Since Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON Regulations are intended solely to determine the outcome of a match when a team's conduct leads the referee to call off the game permanently, they are therefore not applicable in this case. In conclusion, the panel considers that in resuming the match, the referee did not err in law."

"The panel acknowledged that the referee had to make a decision in an atmosphere of extreme tension. However, these circumstances do not justify describing the decision as 'arbitrary.' On the contrary, the Referee's judgment did not appear to have been affected by factors external to the game."

Why was AFCON 2026 final result overturned?

Deep in stoppage time of the 2026 Africa Cup of Nations final, with the score still unblemished, Congolese referee Jean-Jacques Ndala Ngambo awarded Morocco a penalty and a chance to win the match.

The decision was made to whistle for a foul on Brahim Diaz by El Hadji Malick Diouf. The Senegal full-back was judged to have pulled Diaz to the ground during a corner.

The match quickly descended into chaos, as Senegal players protested in full voice. Manager Pape Thiaw summoned his players to the sideline and encouraged them to leave the field of play, apparently in protest. After a few minutes of arguments on the touchline, the team headed down the tunnel to the locker rooms, with the exception of captain Sadio Mane.

Eventually, Mane was able to recall the group back out onto the pitch to continue the game, and goalkeeper Edouard Mendy saved Diaz's penalty. The game went to extra time, and Senegal would emerge as winners after Pape Gueye scored a 94th-minute goal.

On March 17, CAF ruled that Senegal were "declared to have forfeited" the 2026 Africa Cup of Nations final , and Morocco were declared winners of the match by a 3-0 default score. The adjudication came as a result of an official appeal by Morocco regarding the result of the match.

CAF ruled that Senegal's decision to leave the pitch to protest a refereeing decision was a violation of Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON regulations, which stated that: "If, for any reason whatsoever, a team withdraws from the competition or does not report for a match, or refuses to play or leaves the ground before the regular end of the match without the authorisation of the referee, it shall be considered loser and shall be eliminated for good from the current competition. The same shall apply for the teams previously disqualified by decision of CAF."

CAF's appeal board argued that by leaving the pitch for more than 10 minutes, Senegal had refused to play, and thus should be eliminated from the competition.

For all intents and purposes, the Court of Arbitration for Sport is the highest court in the land for these decisions.

However, there could be one avenue left for Morocco and CAF to pursue if they wish to continue this fight.

The only appeal remaining for Morocco is to the Swiss Federal Court, which they could legally pursue. However, this appeal would be on procedural grounds only and would not be heard on the facts or substance of the case itself.

According to multiple reports right before the CAS decision was revealed on Tuesday, including from French journalist Romain Molina , there was a phone call between Senegal FA president Abdoulaye Fall and Ulrich Haas, one of the three CAS judges. This could potentially constitute a legal quagmire, as CAS arbitors are meant to be completely impartial in these cases.

It's unclear at this point if Morocco wish to pursue this legal avenue.

articles.title: Is Ohio State tough enough to beat Michigan on Saturday
articles.summary: Former Ohio State coach Urban Meyer says The Game comes down to toughness when talking at an event where they previewed the contest vs. Michigan.
articles.body:
By almost every account, this has been one of the most disappointing seasons in the history of Ohio State football. Sure, the Buckeyes have fallen short of expectations before, but maybe not in this spectacular fashion.

Ryan Day 's club came into the season ranked as the No. 1 team in the land but couldn't hold onto a 20-point fourth-quarter lead at Texas . After rattling off five straight wins, it seemed that the team had put that loss in the past and was moving in the right direction. Then came the injury to quarterback Julian Sayin , and the wheels fell off. We've never seen a quarterback go down and affect the defense so much. Since the Sayin injury, the defense has allowed 30 points to USC , 41 to Oregon , 19 to Northwestern, and 31 to Nebraska . Unthinkable for the Silver Bullets. Maybe Curt Cignetti's arrogant comments were right ... Maybe Indiana did rip the heart out of the Buckeyes when Sayin got hurt against the Hoosiers.

With the season all but lost, there remain just two tangible goals left: Get Jeremiah Smith the Heisman he deserves and beat Michigan . At this point in the season, fans are a lot more hopeful about the first goal on the list. Recently, Urban Meyer was asked about The Game. As someone who knows a thing or two about this great rivalry, he had some telling comments that will only fuel concern on the side of Buckeye Nation.

Ohio State opens up as a 10-11.5-point favorite , depending on who you ask. That seems like a large margin considering the way both teams played in the past week. Despite the unimpressive record, the Wolverine defense is really good. They play tough, hard-hitting football. It's a defense that just held previously unbeaten UCLA to just 13 points. And Meyer knows that could be a real issue for this year's version of Scarlet and Gray.

"The best unit performing right now is a Wolverine defense, and that concerns me a little bit," Meyer said. "Our offense has been up and down a little bit, and now we're down to our backup quarterback. So I see this being a very low-scoring game. This is Ohio State-Wolverine football. The toughest team is going to win the game."

You can see Meyer's comments below with Jim Tressel nodding along.

Meyer rightfully adds that Michigan's offense has been really bad, calling it "pathetic ," but notes that the Maize and Blue have been in every game because of that tough defense. These are not comforting words just days before battle will take place on the field.

So the question remains: with nothing left to play for other than pride, are the Buckeyes tough enough to win this game? There is no doubt they are the more talented team on paper, but can they prove it on the field of play? Judging from the past four weeks, it's hard to give a resounding yes. All we can hope for at this point is that this Ohio State team shows up with something to prove in a game that will help soothe the pain of an otherwise disappointing season.

articles.title: Where do Patriots currently stand in playoff picture in Week 12?
articles.summary: The Patriots' playoff chances have taken a hit with Drake Maye out, but the team is still firmly in the playoff hunt with seven weeks left to play.
articles.body:
The New England Patriots enter Week 12 of the 2026 NFL season positioned as the No. 8 seed in the AFC with a 5-5 record, remaining just outside of the conference's seven-team playoff field. With several games left on the schedule, New England still has an opportunity to make a postseason push down the final stretch of the season.

The Pittsburgh Steelers currently hold the seventh and final playoff spot in the AFC at 6-4, putting them one game ahead of the Patriots . New England is also within striking distance of the Cleveland Browns , who also sit at 6-4 on the year.

However, a sharp vicissitude in the standings has the chance to take shape, as the Patriots own the tiebreaker over the Steelers after New England defeated Pittsburgh 20-3 in Week 2. They also have the advantage over the Browns, as the Patriots own a better record against AFC opponents (5-1) than the Browns do (4-3). A strong run over the coming weeks in accordance with a slump from either the Steelers or Browns could quickly move the Patriots into playoff positioning.

However, New England faces a significant obstacle following the loss of quarterback Drake Maye, who is expected to miss at least six weeks with a fractured fibula. His absence is expected to considerably dampen the team's chances of mounting a sustained postseason push. However, the Patriots are expected get multiple players back from injured reserve soon, with Alijah Vera-Tucker and Romeo Doubs on track to come back in the coming weeks.

The road ahead for the Patriots includes a meeting with the Los Angeles Chargers on the road in Week 12 before hosting the Buffalo Bills in Week 13 and the Minnesota Vikings in Week 14. Those matchups will be crucial for the team and its postseason outlook, particularly with Buffalo and Minnesota being two of the best teams in the league.
